drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs Decrease Accounted for in the Budget
drivers.description: Decreases funding for Overseas Operations costs. Detailed justifications are provided in the Operation and Maintenance, Air Force Volume III Book.

drivers.title: Airlift Operations - Transportation Working Capital Fund
drivers.description: Decrease represents normalization of Transportation Working Capital Fund rates due to FY 2022 Out-of-Cycle rate increase as a result of increased fuel costs. FY 2023 request takes into account a lower fuel rate than the FY 2022 Enacted position requiring less cost augmentation for the Transportation Working Capital Fund. Airlift Readiness Account -$25,062 (FY 2022 Baseline $212,889) Operational Support Airlift -$45,764 (FY 2022 Baseline $374,012)

drivers.title: Mobility Support Activities - Senior Leader Communication Upgrade
drivers.description: Increase to enhance communications by providing commercial Satellite Communication (SATCOM) capability. Services assure redundant, reliable, and robust secure and non-secure data, voice and video, Presidential Video Teleconferencing (VTC) and continuous real time situational awareness. Increase also allows Air Force Mobility Support Activities to continue to maintain a steady state of operations due to rising costs as a result of continued supply chain variability and consumer demand on products and services.

drivers.title: Airlift Mission Training - Intra Theater Airlift
drivers.description: Increase to airlift portfolio to support increased U.S. Transportation Command (USTRANSCOM) rates due to fuel rate increases. Fuel rates increased by 9% from FY 2022.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Average Workyear Cost Adjustment
drivers.description: Decrease in civilian personnel compensation reflects adjusted average workyear costs. Each year Air Force uses detailed execution and cost factor analysis to update civilian compensation costs for the purpose of accurately forecasting budget estimates for the civilian workforce. The SAG average cost adjustment is a result of these cost changes as well as updated pay raise, awards and benefit assumptions.

drivers.title: Dynamic Campaigning - Tanker Operations
drivers.description: Increase in funding supports dynamic campaigning operational activities across the Indo-Pacific theater. The funding will be used to meet Secretary of Defense (SEDEF), Indo-Pacific Command (INDOPACOM), and Pacific Air Force (PACAF) posture initiatives by enabling fighter, bomber, mobility, tanker and Intelligence Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) operations across the western Pacific. These operations ensures the right capabilities are in the right places at the right time to deliver integrated deterrence towards our adversaries in the Pacific. Additionally, these operations improve interoperability in conjunction with sister services, interagency, and coalition partners by enabling unique scenarios to improve warfighting advantages. Funding provides distributed footprint with allies and partners, logistics that are postured to sustain operations, the ability to synchronize all domain effects, and a persistent combat presence in key locations.

drivers.title: Federal Contractor $15 Per Hour Minimum Wage
drivers.description: Additional funding to address the estimated impacts of Executive Order (E.O.) 14026, Increasing the Minimum Wage for Federal Contractors, dated April 27, 2021. E.O. 14026, Section 4(a) requires the Department of Labor to implement regulations to increase the minimum wage to $15 per hour by January 30, 2022, on contracts covered by the Fair Labor Standards Act, the Service Contract Act (SCA), or the Davis Bacon Act (DBA). The E.O. also applies only to Federal Contractors and Subcontractors on new contract actions entered into on or after January 30, 2022.

drivers.title: Airlift Mission Training - Multi-Capable Airman (MCA) Training
drivers.description: Increase for equipment and training resources for the Multi-Capable Airman (MCA) training program for 10 classes of 40-60 personnel annually. Syllabus and advanced expeditionary requirements are identified by the force providers and combat commanders. MCA requires technology and ground assets that are light, lean and agile to combat against anti-access/area denial situations. Funding will train and educate Airmen for a broad spectrum of expeditionary operations. Skills obtained translate to generating combat missions in contested environments across Air Force Specialty Codes (AFSCs).

drivers.title: Mobility Airlift Forces - Aircraft Retrofit Efficiency
drivers.description: Increase in funding to improve efficiency on existing aircraft through improved engine foam wash, blade coating, and engine blade scanning. Improve energy efficiency on existing aircraft by improving supply chains and energy education.

drivers.title: Operational Communications - Enterprise Information Technology as a Service
drivers.description: Increase funds the transformational modernization of the Department of the Air Force (DAF) information technology infrastructure that will provide integrated security of devices and incorporate Identity, Credential and Access Management (ICAM) and Zero Trust principles down to the user level. Funding will support local base connectivity, remote access, and voice “as a Service” which are part of the DAF’s Enterprise Information Technology as a Service (EITaaS) program. The funding further provides resilient and modernized network connectivity for Base Area Networks (BAN) providing intra-base connectivity for DAF bases to enhance mission effectiveness. The objective of EITaaS is to leverage commercial best practices and provide standardized, innovative and agile IT services across the DAF, as well as improve performance and reliability. The efforts began as a pilot program at a select number of bases to prove out the "as a service" concept, and is now shifting to provide enterprise wide capabilities through the expansion of risk reduction pilot programs to deliver services across the DAF. EITaaS provides modern and agile end device security capabilities and the digital foundation to support the Joint All Domain Command and Control (JADC2) and Advanced Battle Management System (ABMS).

drivers.title: Base Support
drivers.description: Funding provides support for installation functions and engineering in support of Air Force installations including the U.S. Air Force Academy. This program sustains missions capability, quality of life, workforce productivity and infrastructure support. Increase allows Air Force Base Support to maintain a steady state of operations due to rising costs as a result of ongoing supply chain variability and consumer demand on products and services.

drivers.title: Ukraine Supplemental Appropriations
drivers.description: Decrease funding for the one-time FY 2022 Ukraine Supplemental Appropriations provided by P.L. 117-103, FY 2022 Consolidated Appropriations Act.

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs Decrease Accounted for in the Budget
drivers.description: Decreases funding for Overseas Operations costs. Detailed justifications are provided in the Operation and Maintenance, Air Force Volume III Book.

drivers.title: Utilities
drivers.description: Increase Utilities program to fund higher costs during the year of execution due to escalating commodity price increases that are outstripping budgeted pricing factors -- OP32: 913 only budgeted at 2.1%. Increase also funds utilities privatization, Energy Savings Performance Contracts, Utility Energy Services Contracts and leased utilities.

drivers.title: Operational Communications - Information Technology
drivers.description: Increase funds delivery of services consisting of secure and non-secure fixed voice communications, wireless voice, data and video connectivity services, and video conferencing services. Provides a wide array of support from infrastructure, collaboration, Desktop Management Support, Service Desk Support, Continuity of Operations and Disaster Recovery support for the end user. Increase allows Air Force Information Technology to maintain a steady state of operations due to rising costs as a result of ongoing supply chain variability and consumer demand on products and services.

drivers.title: Operational Communications - Data Fabric
drivers.description: Increase provides funding to assist in establishing Department of the Air Force Data Fabric. It will be used to enhance mission and business operations by making data visible, accessible, usable, linked, trusted, interoperable, and secure. This enterprise investment accelerates the data backbone and data informed decisions as part of the Air Force's digital transformation.

drivers.title: Military Personnel and Dependent Support - Minimum Wage Increase
drivers.description: Decrease in funding following one-time increase provided in P.L. 117-103, FY 2022 Consolidated Appropriations Act for minimum wage increase for non-appropriated fund employees.

drivers.title: Base Operations Support - Unified Combatant Command Support
drivers.description: Increase funding to support Combatant Command tasked operational exercises, non-contingency related deployments and dynamic force employment. Funding will support unit deployments, base maintenance contracts, pavement clearance, snow removal and base information technology infrastructures. Increase will further expand funding for staff functions, contracting, drayage and beddown programs for Department of Defense tenants and management analysis.

drivers.title: Operational Communications - Information Technology Spend Study
drivers.description: Increase provides funds to support the Department of the Air Force goal toward making significant investments to deliver digital infrastructure necessary to ultimately dominate the information domain in a contested cyberspace environment. Enables a high performance team to make recommendations and implement a fully functioning, highly-effective Enterprise Information Technology management structure, incorporating repeatable resource efficiency mechanisms for dollars and manpower.

drivers.title: Federal Contractor $15 Per Hour Minimum Wage
drivers.description: Additional funding to address the estimated impacts of Executive Order (E.O.) 14026, Increasing the Minimum Wage for Federal Contractors, dated April 27, 2021. E.O. 14026, Section 4(a) requires the Department of Labor to implement regulations to increase the minimum wage to $15 per hour by January 30, 2022, on contracts covered by the Fair Labor Standards Act, the Service Contract Act (SCA), or the Davis Bacon Act (DBA). The E.O. also applies only to Federal Contractors and Subcontractors on new contract actions entered into on or after January 30, 2022.

drivers.title: Operational Communications - Cloud One
drivers.description: Increase for cloud capacity, sustainment labor and migration costs to migrate additional applications to Cloud One and sustain applications after migration. Cloud One standardizes platforms and application support services providing secured cloud environments, engineered environments and cyber security solutions for 2,700+ mission applications.

drivers.title: Operational Communications - Air Force Africa Antiterrorism/Force Protection
drivers.description: Increase for network services to enhance base defense, perimeter security, indirect fire protection, communications and intelligence support for improved interoperability and data sharing across Cooperative Security Locations (CSLs) across Air Forces Africa locations. Increase mitigates shortfalls for the Antiterrorism/Force Protection program at CSLs and mitigates vulnerabilities. This is a continuation of the efforts that began in FY 2022 and brings the program to a steady state.

drivers.title: Child and Youth Programs - Fee Assistance for Active Duty Child Care
drivers.description: Increase expands existing resources to fully fund Service child care fee assistance programs for Active Duty personnel. This critical mission capability provides child care support for military families to ensure readiness of our Airmen is ensured. This program has historically continues to expand, the Department of the Air Force documented an increase of demand at a rate of 29% from FY 2021 to FY 2022.

drivers.title: Facility Operations Support
drivers.description: Increase continues to support Facilities Operations for mission-critical functions and better align funding with actual execution. Increase funds BMCs to the minimum level of service and keeps pace with increased costs for service related activities. This increase supports Air Force-wide real property leasing, easements and local airfield usage, and Base Maintenance Contracts (BMCs). BMCs include firefighting, utilities management and commodities production, pest management, community planning, real property management, engineering services, pavement clearance (sweeping and snow removal) and Emergency Management.

drivers.title: Child and Youth Programs - Cloud Based Data Systems for Child Care
drivers.description: Increase upgrades existing Service child care data management systems, including cloud-based data storage and connectivity. This enables the Department of the Air Force's ability to access real-time data to effectively utilize critical Child Care space requirements, improved wait list monitoring and establish improved enterprise wide decision support on resourcing for child and youth programs.

drivers.title: Supply and Transportation Logistics - Electrical Vehicle Programs
drivers.description: Decrease funding following one-time increase provided in P.L. 117-103, FY 2022 Consolidated Appropriations Act for Air Force Electrical Vehicle Programs.

drivers.title: Base Operations Support - Personal Protective Equipment
drivers.description: Increase to support COVID Task Force request to increase medical and non-medical personal protective equipment (PPE) to ensure sufficient capacity is available and to meet medical equipment needs across the Total Force in anticipation of a future pandemic. Task Force recommends funding PPE stocks to eliminate forecasted shortfalls, enabling Department of Defense to ensure workforce safety and a robust medical response to emerging threats.

drivers.title: Base Operations Support - Red Hill
drivers.description: Decrease in funding following one-time increase provided in P.L. 117-103, FY 2022 Consolidated Appropriations Act for Red Hill contamination clean up.

drivers.title: Facilities Operations Support - Cyber Resiliency
drivers.description: Decrease in funding following one-time increase provided in P.L. 117-103, Consolidated Appropriations Act for cyber resiliency for Nuclear Command, Control, and Communications bases.

drivers.title: Zero Emission Vehicles
drivers.description: Increase provides funding to lease 14,087 non-tactical electric vehicles, while simultaneously reducing the total non-tactical vehicle fleet by a total of 5,635 vehicles across the FYDP to support improved climate and accelerated energy resilience due to changing climate that will continue to amplify operational demands on the force. Funding will also support vehicle charging station infrastructure planning and procuring telematics data on fleet use. Major Programs: Facilities Operations Support +$4,942 (FY 2022 Base: 1,056,842) Supply and Transportation Logistics +$2,400 (FY 2022 Base: $328,499)

drivers.title: Base Security and Law Enforcement - Royal Air Force Lakenheath
drivers.description: Increase for classified program. Classified information will be delivered with classified Operation and Maintenance justification materials.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Exceptional Family Member Program Standardization
drivers.description: Increase provides half-year funding and manpower (21 FTEs) and second half-year funding for 83 FTEs received in FY 2022 to support the Exceptional Family Member Program (EFMP) and ensure adequate service to 36.3K Airmen and 54K special needs family members. This action supports resiliency, retention, and readiness of Airmen by connecting EFMP family members to critical medical, educational, and family support resources.

drivers.title: Operational Communications
drivers.description: Increase for mission critical Operational Communications functions which includes additional Land Mobile Radio systems, voice, backup power, cable and antenna maintenance and repairs. This funding accelerates the service's capability to bring communication infrastructure to industry standard, improves reliability for delivery of information technology and Command and Control capabilities.

drivers.title: Airfield Operations Support - Dispersal Site Kits
drivers.description: Increase funds the United States Air Forces in Europe's airfield operations equipment requirement for Agile Combat Employment (ACE) forward operating sites. Funding enables operations in austere environments employing rapid and resilient airpower. Additional program details are classified and will be provided under separate cover with the classified Operation and Maintenance justification materials.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Average Workyear Cost Adjustment
drivers.description: Decrease in civilian personnel compensation reflects adjusted average workyear costs. Each year Air Force uses detailed execution and cost factor analysis to update civilian compensation costs for the purpose of accurately forecasting budget estimates for the civilian workforce. The SAG average cost adjustment is a result of these cost changes as well as updated pay raise, awards and benefit assumptions.

drivers.title: Operational Communications - Adobe Joint Enterprise License Agreement
drivers.description: Increase funds the per license price increase for the follow-on Adobe Joint Enterprise License Agreement III (JELA-III). The Adobe JELA-III is a multi-year contract the leverages the buying power of 2.6 million Department of Defense and Defense Health Agency personnel to reduce costs, improve interoperability, expand collaborations, enhance document services, and extend publishing and creative capabilities.

drivers.title: Child and Youth Programs - Child Care Provider Rate Cap
drivers.description: Increase provides funding Child Care Provider Rate Cap. Adds funds to resource all fee active duty dependent child care assistance programs at the $1,700 provider rate cap. Fully funds the Air Force at the Department of Defense directed maximum rate.

drivers.title: Child and Youth Programs - Childcare Fee
drivers.description: Decrease funding due to one-time increase provided in P.L. 117-103, FY 2022 Consolidated Appropriations for childcare fees due to increased family participation in childcare programs.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Medical Administration
drivers.description: Increase provides half-year funding and manpower in Base Support (Subactivity Group 11Z $2,255, 14 FTE), Mobilization Preparedness (Subactivity 21D $7,836, 103 FTEs), Administration (Subactivity Group 42A $1,859, 30 FTEs) and Other Service Wide Activities (Subactivity Group 42G $6,157, 105 FTEs) to support medical administration positions with civilians.

drivers.title: Airfield Operations Support - Regional Base Cluster Pre-Position Kits
drivers.description: Increase for Regional Base Cluster Pre-position (RBCP) kits. RBCP kits provide a survivable, adaptive solution to the risk of forward basing through prepositioning combat support and base operating support equipment at dispersed Agile Combat Employment (ACE) locations throughout the theater. RBCPs reduce the need for airlift requirements to transport expeditionary operations such as rapid runway repair material, power generators and communication gears. Additional program details are classified and will be provided under separate cover with the classified Operation and Maintenance justification materials.

drivers.title: General Skills Training
drivers.description: Increase in travel, supplies, and training instructors to support the Air Force Education and Training Command (AETC) mission of providing the necessary skills and training required for Airmen to provide optimal performance in their profession and the field of battle. Increase funding continues to support significant backlog of necessary training, while steadily normalizing training flow, that has occurred over the last two fiscal years.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Average Workyear Cost Adjustment
drivers.description: Increase in civilian personnel compensation reflects adjusted average workyear costs. Each year Air Force uses detailed execution and cost factor analysis to update civilian compensation costs for the purpose of accurately forecasting budget estimates for the civilian workforce. The SAG average cost adjustment is a result of these cost changes as well as updated pay raise, awards and benefit assumptions.

drivers.title: Specialized Skills Training - Joint All-Domain Command and Control Training
drivers.description: Increase for Joint All-Domain Command and Control (JADC2) training to establish an Intelligence Formal Training Unit (IFTU) . JADC2 training is required to deliver the well-trained and experienced Airmen the Air Force needs for multi-domain operations. Increase continues to support modernizing the JADC2 training course to formats that multi-domain training capability enhancement across Intelligence, Cyber Space Warfighting, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) disciplines that began in FY2022

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - General Skills Training
drivers.description: Increase provides full-year funding and manpower (19 FTEs) to support the Air Force Education and Training Command (AETC) mission of providing the necessary skills and training required for Airmen in their profession and the field of battle. Additional instructors and support staff will help resolve significant backlog of necessary general skills training.

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs Decrease Accounted for in the Budget
drivers.description: Decreases funding for Overseas Operations costs. Detailed justifications are provided in the Operation and Maintenance, Air Force Volume III Book.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Joint All Domain C2 Training DAWN
drivers.description: Increase provides half-year funding and manpower for FY 2023 (2 FTEs) and the second half-year funding (12 FTEs) added in FY 2022 to modernize Joint All Domain Command and Control training from “stove-piped” to “Multi-Domain” training delivered in a mission context.

drivers.title: Federal Contractor $15 Per Hour Minimum Wage
drivers.description: Additional funding to address the estimated impacts of Executive Order (E.O.) 14026, Increasing the Minimum Wage for Federal Contractors, dated April 27, 2021. E.O. 14026, Section 4(a) requires the Department of Labor to implement regulations to increase the minimum wage to $15 per hour by January 30, 2022, on contracts covered by the Fair Labor Standards Act, the Service Contract Act (SCA), or the Davis Bacon Act (DBA). The E.O. also applies only to Federal Contractors and Subcontractors on new contract actions entered into on or after January 30, 2022.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Nuclear Certification Program Transfer
drivers.description: Increase transfers full-year funding and manpower from the Air Force, Research, Development, Training & Education appropriation to Air Force, Operations and Maintenance, Specialized Skill Training (Subactivity Group 32A $182, 2 FTEs), This puts manpower directly in units performing the nuclear certification program mission.

drivers.title: Airlift Mission Training - Airlift Readiness Account
drivers.description: Decrease is part of the realignment of resources to support necessary capability investments in accordance with the National Defense Strategy. The Air Force will coordinate with USTRANSCOM to reduce year-of-execution budgetary shortfalls.

drivers.title: Airlift Mission Training - Training Test and Ferry
drivers.description: Decrease impacts Air Mobility Command's Training, Test, and Ferry mission by assuming risk in the wartime mobility proficiency requirements and local readiness training hours.

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs - Operation Enduring Sentinel
drivers.description: Decrease funds for airlift mission training in support of OES Missions. This impacts airlift support training for Air Mobility Command and is a part of the realignment of resources to support necessary capability investments in accordance with the National Defense Strategy.

drivers.title: Airlift Mission Training - Operational Support Airlift
drivers.description: Decrease assumes risk in the movement of support packages (communications equipment, security details, vehicles) accompanying distinguished visitors during worldwide travel.

drivers.title: Mobility Support Activities - Senior Leader Communication Upgrade
drivers.description: Decrease following prior year programmatic increase to enhance communications by providing commercial Satellite Communication (SATCOM) capability. These services assure redundant, reliable, and robust secure and non-secure data, voice and video, Presidential video teleconferencing, and continuous real time situational awareness.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Average Workyear Cost Adjustment
drivers.description: Increase in Civilian Personnel compensation adjusts average workyear costs. Each year, Air Force uses detailed execution and cost factor analysis to update civilian compensation costs for the purpose of accurately forecasting budget estimates for the civilian workforce. The Subactivity Group average cost adjustment is a result of these cost changes as well as updated pay raise, awards and benefit assumptions.

drivers.title: Mobility Airlift Forces - Agility Prime
drivers.description: Decrease following one-time programmatic increase for Agility Prime. Agility Prime will utilize electric vertical takeoff-and-landing (eVTOL) vehicles to move personnel and equipment. Prior year funding supported aircraft lease and interim contractor support to allow the Air Force to assess the viability of the aircraft.

drivers.title: Tanker Operations - Dynamic Campaigning
drivers.description: Decrease following one-time programmatic increase for dynamic campaigning operational activities across the Indo-Pacific theater. Prior year funding was used to address Secretary of Defense (SEDEF), Indo-Pacific Command (INDOPACOM), and Pacific Air Force (PACAF) posture initiatives by enabling fighter, bomber, mobility, tanker and Intelligence Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) operations across the western Pacific.

drivers.title: Airlift Mission Training - Multi-Capable Airmen
drivers.description: Increase to support Multi-Capable Airman (MCA) training program. Program is designed to utilize Agile Combat Employment concepts that will efficiently develop, train, and employ Airmen to support and solve problems with the resources at hand. It emphasizes Airmen training outside their primary career field and as part of a cross-functional team. Airmen will be trained in topics such as combat and medical care to ensure a dynamic force. Funds will be used to obtain equipment and training resources to educate Airmen for broad spectrum of expeditionary operations.

drivers.title: Airlift Mission Training - Reversal of C-5M Divestment
drivers.description: Increase to reverse divestiture of C-5M fleet and assist in retaining aircraft inventory profile. Funds will help maintain mission training requirements while supporting Training, Test, and Ferry (TTF) C-5 channel mission. Funding the fleet will help close the strategic airlift and special transport gaps that would result from the divestment of the C-5s.

drivers.title: Airlift Mission Training - Energy Efficiency Software
drivers.description: Increase to enhance Combat Capability and mitigate operational risk to the warfighter through energy-informed solutions and technology. Energy efficiency software funding addresses the United States Air Force requirement to increase readiness of the force and reduce demand on operation energy. The investments accelerate the operations and maintenance of technologies that improve training and readiness including training operations modeling, advanced distributed operations, and the pilot training next learning environment.

drivers.title: Operational Support Airlift
drivers.description: Decrease Operational Support Airlift to better align funding to execution.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Full-Time Equivalents Adjustment
drivers.description: Decrease adjusts Civilian full-time equivalents. Each year, Air Force uses detailed execution to update civilian full-time equivalents for the purpose of accurately forecasting budget estimates for the civilian workforce. The Subactivity Group full-time equivalents adjustment is a result of these changes.

drivers.title: Operational Communications - Enterprise Service Agreement
drivers.description: Increase in funding to support the new Navy-led Enterprise Service Agreement contract, which consolidates the Joint Enterprise License Agreement (JELA) and Department of the Air Force 365 (DAF365) requirement. The contract creates a single funding line for cloud hosted business applications, security, and required software for day-to-day business. Also, this will fund Enterprise Infrastructure Solutions (EIS) SharePoint, Enterprise Information Technology Service Desk, Windows 10 Secure Host Baseline, along with Microsoft Defender for Servers and Endpoints. This will fulfill the mandated security licensing from Department of Defense Chief Information Office and U.S. Cyber Command.

drivers.title: Operational Communications - Voice Session Border Controller and TDM Circuit Transitions
drivers.description: Increase will support the transition of legacy voice services and telephony from time division multiplex (TDM) infrastructure to voice over internet protocol infrastructure (VOIP). This upgrade will mitigate risk due to unsupported, aging technology and equipment, as well as a growing technical debt caused by keeping this outdated technology operational. Funding will provide local session controller equipment at each base and regional session border controller equipment to allow Department of the Air Force (DAF) voice traffic to stay within the DAF network avoiding Defense Information System Agency related costs. Furthermore, TDM is not compatible with emergency 911 mandates, puts safety of life at risk, and will incur county and state penalties for not being in line with emergency 911 standards. This funding will also support transition of legacy service contracts, buys down fees due to end of life/vendor non-support and required state 911 integration mandates, and takes advantage of readily available Defense Information Services Agency (DISA) Voice services to expedite transition.

drivers.title: Operational Communications - Zero Trust Cybersecurity Protocols
drivers.description: Increase funds Zero Trust programs to transform current network boundary-focused cybersecurity capabilities. Zero Trust accelerates the Department of the Air Force into next generation warfare by simplifying digital access, without sacrificing security. This data and resource access strategy falls squarely on the Advanced Battle Management Systems (ABMS) critical path, which makes the warfighting changes necessary to evolve as a service.

drivers.title: Zero Emission Vehicles Program
drivers.description: Increase to vehicle lease program to lease non-tactical electric vehicles and increases to facilities operations to install electric vehicle charging stations. Funds additional infrastructure, service contracts, sustainment, program management, innovation and analysis to advance the Air Force's Electric Vehicle program. Initiative mitigates future climate impacts and meets direction in accordance with Department of Defense and Department of the Air Force climate action plans. Major Programs: Supply and Transportation Logistics +$2,533 (FY 2023 Base: $305,255) Facilities Operations Support +$90,000 (FY 2023 Base: $1,102,411)

drivers.title: Operational Communications - Enterprise Information Technology as a Service
drivers.description: Increase in the Enterprise Information Technology as a Service (EITaaS) provides funding to start scaling Wave 1 End User Services and Base Infrastructure Modernization (BIM) enterprise wide. EITaaS Wave 1 will scale the Information Technology (IT) service management platform, enterprise service desk and endpoint management solution to up to 400,000 Department of the Air Force users. BIM will scale from four bases in Fiscal Year (FY) 2023 to a total of 17 bases by FY 2024.

drivers.title: Military Personnel and Dependent Support - Food Service Operations
drivers.description: Increase to Food Service 2.0 program and extends Campus Dining availability. Funds mess attendant contracts; provides Campus Dining for Outside the Continental United States (OCONUS) and 25 Continental United States (CONUS) bases with specialized Dining Facilities contracts. Funding increases food delivery models to include expanded menus, access and availability to meals, and healthier food options. Recapitalize dining facility furniture, fixtures and equipment that is beyond expected life cycle for replacement. Food Service 2.0 performance will be reported to Office of Secretary of Defense and Congress annually.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Full-Time Equivalents and Average Workyear Cost Adjustment
drivers.description: Increase in Civilian Personnel compensation adjusts full-time equivalents and average workyear costs. Each year, Air Force uses detailed execution and cost factor analysis to update civilian compensation costs for the purpose of accurately forecasting budget estimates for the civilian workforce. The Subactivity Group full-time equivalents and average cost adjustment is a result of these changes as well as updated pay raise, awards and benefit assumptions.

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs - Operation Enduring Sentinel - Base Operations Support
drivers.description: Decrease funds to base operations support in support of Operation Enduring Sentinel missions. This impacts command support to tactical, mobility, and strategic air forces for Department of the Air Force locations in the CENTCOM AOR and is a part of the realignment of resources to support necessary capability investments in accordance with the National Defense Strategy.

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs - Operation Enduring Sentinel - Facilities Operations Support
drivers.description: Decrease funds to facilities operations support in support of Operation Enduring Sentinel missions. This specifically impacts facility support for tactical air forces for Department of the Air Force locations in the CENTCOM AOR and is a part of the realignment of resources to support necessary capability investments in accordance with the National Defense Strategy.

drivers.title: Child and Youth Programs
drivers.description: Increase to support Child and Youth fee assistance programs, family resiliency contracts, recapitalization of information technology facility with upgraded furniture, fixtures and equipment. Also ensures adequate operating supplies for daily requirements.

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs - Operation Enduring Sentinel - Operational Communication
drivers.description: Decrease funds for operational communications in support of Operation Enduring Sentinel missions. This impacts command support for tactical air forces, Enterprise IT projects and connections. This reduction is a part of the realignment of resources to support necessary capability investments in accordance with the National Defense Strategy.

drivers.title: Operational Communications - Cyber Sensor
drivers.description: Increase funds cyber sensors to gain situational awareness of the cyber threat. This will fund the capability to increase Commanders and warfighters ability to see, characterize, and respond to potential cyber threats. Funding will be used to identify priority gaps and vulnerabilities in the Department's ability to transition to and support current and projected operational plans in a contested environment.

drivers.title: Operational Communications - Artificial Intelligence/Machine Language Readiness
drivers.description: Increase provides funding for Department of the Air Force investments for data-driven decisions, Artificial Intelligence, readiness, and decision advantage on an enterprise scale. Provides shared foundational data services, enterprise-wide warfighter/business-health decision making platforms through an Information Technology tech stack. This a key initiative for readiness analysis, requirements, full audits, Artificial Intelligence/Machine Language readiness and use.

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs - Operation Enduring Sentinel - Utilities
drivers.description: Decrease in utilities supporting the 5 main operating locations and 6 supporting locations in the CENTCOM AOR. This decrease is a part of the realignment of resources to support necessary capability investments in accordance with the National Defense Strategy.

drivers.title: Facilities Operations Support - Base Operating Support Contract
drivers.description: Decrease to Base Operating Support and Base Maintenance contracts for 31 bases. A large spectrum of services will be reduced to include installation engineering, real property management, emergency management, fire and emergency services, environmental support, grounds maintenance, solid waste management and custodial services. In an effort to support higher priority Air Force bills, and due to the structure of Base Operating Support contracts, installations will see a reduction of contract manpower of approximately 20-30 percent.

drivers.title: Operational Communications - Cybersecurity for Network Component Purchases
drivers.description: Increase funds migration tools to protect the Air Force network against vulnerabilities which would allow adversaries to gain control of devices, divert traffic, intercept sensitive information, and cause denial of services attacks. These vulnerabilities were discovered in a Fiscal Year 2019 audit and Fiscal Year 2021 validation audit. This will fund Secretary of the Air Force approved Management Initiative capability to address Audit and Material weaknesses.

drivers.title: Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substance Environmental Response and Remediation
drivers.description: Increase funds response to Per and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) impacted drinking water at/near 189 current/closed installations and locations, determines AF responsibility, conducts investigations, and response actions to provide safe drinking water. Purges hangar fire suppression systems/firetrucks to retrofit or install new systems w/new approved replacement foam. Major Programs: Facilities Operations Support +$4,000 (FY 2023 Base: $948,758) Environmental Quality +$10,500 (FY 2023 Base: $297,611)

drivers.title: Environmental Quality - Aqueous Film Forming Foam Removal and Disposal
drivers.description: Decrease in funding following one-time increase provided in P.L. 117-328, FY 2023 Consolidated Appropriations Act for removal and disposal of Aqueous Film Forming Foam.

drivers.title: Child and Youth Programs - Child Development Program Employee Tuition Support

drivers.description: Decrease funds for base operations requirements requirements in support of Other Theater missions.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Child Care Workforce
drivers.description: Increase full-year funding and manpower (121 FTEs) to accelerate the implementation of and hiring for Lead Educator and Special Needs Inclusion Coordinator programs. This continues and accelerates a successful initiative begun in the FY2025 budget. Additionally, the program increases the discount available to child care providers at DoD facilities from 50% to 100% for their first child enrolled and adds a 25% discount for their second child enrolled.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Navy to Air Force - Joint Base Pearl Harbor Hickam
drivers.description: Increase full-year funding and manpower (129 FTEs) to transfer funding and civilian FTEs from the Navy (Supporting Component) to the Air Force (Supported Component) for the Logistics Readiness Squadron (LRS) and the Equal Employment Opportunity/Equal Opportunity (EEO/EO) installation support functions at Joint Base Pearl Harbor Hickam (JBPHH), Hawaii, consistent with the Installation Support Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) for JBPHH.

drivers.title: Operational Communications - Data Fabric
drivers.description: Increase provides critical funding for essential warfighting capabilities, driving efficiency, and delivering a decisive decision advantage. Establishes a strong, shared foundational data service environment, contributing to timely, relevant, and actionable information, extending from the strategic level to the tactical edge. Enables seamless integration of data and capabilities, creating a cohesive and interconnected operational environment, enhancing abilities to sense, decide, and act with speed and precision, supporting the success of global operations.

drivers.title: Child and Youth Programs - Child Care Workforce
drivers.description: Increase in program funding to provide discounts for child care providers at DoD facilities from 50% to 100% for their first child and 25% discount for a second child enrolled. Child care workforce initiatives increase and sustain manning levels at Child and Youth facilities to best provide Service members with affordable and quality childcare which is critical to mission readiness.

drivers.title: Facilities Operations Support - Active Protection and Reconnaissance Platform
drivers.description: Decrease following a one-time 2025 Congressional mark increase to provide funding support for critical programs increasing active protection for base personnel and projects enhancing reconnaissance platforms.

drivers.title: Base Operations Support - Wi-Fi in Unaccompanied Housing (UH)
drivers.description: Increase in program funding to support the standup of free Wi-Fi in UH for military members. Funding in FY2026 and FY2027 will prioritize the initial startup and installation fees associated with the standup of providing WiFi service within dorms and barracks. Funding in future years will be recurring to provide for service and maintenance fees and any additional sustainment costs of the program.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Army to Air Force - Joint Base Lewis-McChord
drivers.description: Increase full-year funding and manpower (65 FTEs) to return resourcing and responsibility from the Army, the supporting Component, to the Air Force, the supported Component.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Child Care Manpower
drivers.description: Increase full-year funding and manpower (70 FTEs) to implement the updated child care provider compensation, reduce low staff to child ratios, and add special needs coordinators within U.S. Air Force Child and Youth Programs.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Weapons Generation Facility Completion
drivers.description: Increase full-year funding and manpower (24 FTEs) to support the implementation of weapons generation facilities, which consolidate weapons storage, maintenance, and training into one building. Functions of the additional manpower include security forces and maintenance needed to complete the construction that will subsequently ensure safe storage of the nuclear arsenal.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Combat Support Equipment Deployment
drivers.description: Increase full-year funding and manpower to (3 FTEs) to support the accelerate change or lose initiative of Agile Combat Employment (ACE). The support will ensure the prototyping, acquisition, and employment of ACE combat support equipment prioritizing a multi- capable force and a more streamlined approach to operations.

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs - Operation Inherent Resolve (OIR)
drivers.description: Increase funds for Supply and Transportation Logistics in support of Operation Inherent Resolve (OIR).

drivers.title: Facilities Operations Support - US IndoPacific Command Yap International Airport, Wake Island
drivers.description: Program execution encountered delays and has slipped from FY2025 to FY2026, funding is still required and the one-time decrease after increase to support acquisition of land for an agreed upon defense site under appropriate international agreement will be delayed one year. Land acquisition is still required to complete the runway extension, parking apron, and taxiway construction at Yap International Airport, Wake Island.

drivers.title: General and Specialized Skills - Initial Technical Training Transformation
drivers.description: Decrease of funds is a result of fiscal year 2024 and 2025 initial investment in Technical Training Transformation efforts in order to infuse agility and enhance readiness and lethality. This ends a two-year dedicated investment to modernize and upgrade classrooms, course curriculum, and teaching structures.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Efficiency - Workforce Optimization
drivers.description: Decrease funding and manpower (60 FTEs) to optimize the workforce in compliance with Executive Order 14210, "Implementing the President's Department of Government Efficiency Workforce Optimization Initiative."

drivers.title: Efficiency - Travel
drivers.description: Reduces discretionary travel funding to align with Executive Order 14222, "Implementing the President's Department of Government Efficiency Cost Efficiency Initiative.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Average Workyear Cost Adjustment
drivers.description: Decrease in funding to for Civilian Personnel compensation adjusts average workyear costs. Each year, the Air Force uses detailed execution and cost factor analysis to realign and update civilian compensation costs and manpower for the purpose of accurately forecasting budget estimates for the civilian workforce. The Subactivity Group average cost adjustment is a result of these changes as well as updated pay raise, awards, and benefit assumptions.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Security Assistance - Misaligned Programs
drivers.description: Decrease full-year funding and manpower (60 FTEs) to eliminate the Aviation Leadership Program, Inter-European Air Forces Academy, U.S. Air Force Europe-Africa's 4th Combat Training Squadron and Combat Training School, 571st Mobility Support Advisory Squadron, 818th Mobility Support Advisory Squadron, 637th International Support Squadron, USAFE/AFAFRICA's 4th Combat Training Squadron.

drivers.title: General Skills Training - 175th Cyber Wing Conversion (Martin State)
drivers.description: Increase of funds to convert the 175th Fighter Wing to a Cyberspace Wing supported by the Secretary of the Air Force basing decision dated March 6, 2024 which codified the transition to the 175th Fighter Wing to a Cyberspace Wing. Funds will be used to purchase equipment in support of mission requirements.

drivers.title: Efficiency - Contract Services
drivers.description: Reduces contracts for Advisory and Assistance Services to promote efficiencies and advance the policies of the Administration in alignment with Executive Order 14222, "Implementing the President's Department of Government Efficiency Cost Efficiency Initiative.

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs - Operation Enduring Sentinel (OES) - Efficiency - Contract Services
drivers.description: Reduces contracts for Advisory and Assistance Services to promote efficiencies and advance the policies of the Administration in alignment with Executive Order 14222, “Implementing the President’s Department of Government Efficiency Cost Efficiency Initiative.”

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs - Operation Enduring Sentinel (OES)
drivers.description: Decrease funds for general skills training supplies in support of OES. This reduction is driven by a decrease in Air Force military deployments with this required training in the U.S. Central Command AOR.

drivers.title: Airlift Readiness Account (ARA)
drivers.description: Increase aligns the FY 2027 funding to the most current USTRANSCOM projections for operating expense shortfalls driven by increased costs from the demand for channel missions that exceed revenue collected from the published working capital fund (WCF) rates and the Joint Services' airlift usage. The WCF rates are set to competitive levels with commercial cargo rates. This increase to the ARA budget allows USTRANSCOM to keep the WCF rates at levels comparable to commercial rates and provide timely service to the warfighters across the globe. Lack of funding in this program will increase costs to the Services requiring airlift support, or a reduction in executable flying hours and cargo transport service availability, which increases risks to pilot's mandatory currency rating and delays the delivery time of personnel, equipment and supplies to warfighters.

drivers.title: Airlift Support Operation and Maintenance (O&M)
drivers.description: Decrease to Airlift Support (O&M) funds aligns programming to anticipated operational tempo for contingency training flying hours. The projected volume of flight operations in-theater directly impacts the aircraft availability and cumulative flying hours required for pilots to meet training requirements. This program provides the highest quality time for aircrews in C-5 and C-17 airframes to maintain war-time proficiency for near peer conflicts, separate from their highly monetized flying to deliver cargo for USTRANSOM mission.

drivers.title: Restore Airlift Operations - Transfer from Discretionary to Mandatory
drivers.description: Reflects an increase in Airlift Operations funding to restore baseline funding levels after a one-time decrease in FY 2026 due to a transfer of discretionary funding to be sourced from the Reconciliation Bill (Public Law No: 119-21 - One Big Beautiful Bill Act).

drivers.title: Senior Leader Communications System
drivers.description: Increase to provide senior leader Command, Control and Communication (C3) capabilities to the nation's senior leaders (e.g. President, Vice President, Secretary of War, Secretary of State, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Combatant Commanders, etc.) while airborne. This budget represents a focus on peace through strength and defense of the homeland by providing secure, reliable communications, constantly while senior leaders are in-transit across the country and around the world, ensuring their ability to maintain situational awareness of information and events in real-time. These C3 capabilities cannot be met by strictly traditional means (e.g. radio) that are vulnerable to modern threats, but through resilient space-based connectivity. The stability of the communications capabilities aboard these aircraft [two VC-25A; four C32A; four C-40B; seven C-40C; sixteen C-37; two Roll-On Conference Capsules/Steel Eagles] directly affects their readiness and availability for the kill chain, and all war-time mission requirements.

drivers.title: Mobile Aircraft Satellite Communication Connectivity
drivers.description: Increase to provide satellite communications connectivity for C-17, KC-135 and KC-46 fleets. These beyond-line-of-site communications capabilities are lifesaving mitigation measures that provide secure, reliable communications (aircraft-to-control center and aircraft-to-aircraft), enabling situational awareness and in-flight coordination, in contested airspace. These service contracts are necessary to ensure in-flight tracking and deconfliction to avoid mishaps and combat losses.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Average Workyear Cost Adjustment
drivers.description: Increase in Civilian Personnel compensation adjusts average workyear costs. Each year the Air Force uses detailed execution and cost factor analysis to update civilian compensation costs for the purpose of accurately forecasting budget estimates for the civilian workforce. The Subactivity Group average cost adjustment is a result of these changes as well as updated pay raise, awards and benefit assumptions.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Workforce Modernization
drivers.description: Increase funding and manpower (65 FTEs) reflects the alignment of civilian staffing to validated mission requirements pursuant to Executive Order 14210, implementing the President’s Department of Government Efficiency Workforce Optimization Initiative and the March 2025 Deputy Secretary of War memorandum. The Air Force conducted comprehensive data-hygiene and manpower-validation efforts, resulting in a correction where FY2026 staffing levels were set below the Airlift Operations Program established requirements. The FY2027 request reflects the full requirement necessary to enable the movement of people, supplies, and equipment to critical locations around the world. Additionally, this program provides opportunities for Air Force pilots and aircrews to gain much needed flight experience which improves readiness.

drivers.title: Efficiency - Contract Services
drivers.description: The reduction of funding for contract services is undertaken in direct support of the President’s executive order, which prioritizes cost efficiency, transparency, and the consolidation of services. This measure represents a deliberate workforce optimization strategy designed to streamline resources while safeguarding against adverse impacts to modernization initiatives and overall mission effectiveness.

drivers.title: Operational Communications - Enterprise Information Technology (EIT) Enterprise Services
drivers.description: Funds support Enterprise IT as a Service (EITaaS), Microsoft 365 and Adobe Enterprise Licenses, Installation Emergency Management, and Unified Capabilities (UC) requirements, addressing historical underfunding of EIT Enterprise Services. EITaaS is the Department of the Air Force's core IT modernization strategy, transitioning bases to a secure, cost-effective, and commercially managed "as-a-service" model. Microsoft 365 provides essential productivity, messaging, and collaboration tools for Airmen and civilians, while the Adobe Enterprise License Agreement delivers 560,000 licenses for secure document creation and management. The UC program replaces outdated analog phone systems with a centralized Voice Over Internet Protocol (VOIP) solution, reducing costs and improving communication security and reliability. This budget ensures Warfighters have the collaborative software, secure IT connectivity, and resilient platforms needed to defend the homeland and deter adversaries.

drivers.title: Operational Communications - Enterprise Information Technology (EIT) Connect
drivers.description: Funds support Defense Information Systems Network (DISN) Infrastructure Services (IS) and Base IT Infrastructure Support requirements. The increase corrects historical underfunding of EIT Connect requirements. The DISN-IS program is the foundational service that ensures network connectivity for all daily Department of the Air Force mission. The Base IT Infrastructure Support program ensures IT infrastructure at DAF locations is sustained and functioning, and replaced as hardware fails, reaches end-of-life, or is rendered obsolete as technology continues to advance. This budget ensures Warfighters have the secure connectivity and resilient IT infrastructure to produce a ready and capable force that can meet National Defense Strategy objectives of defending the homeland and deterring China (and other adversaries).

drivers.title: Efficiency - Supplies and Materials
drivers.description: Reduces funding for supplies and materials to align with historical execution levels and ensure alignment with the priorities of the Secretary of War to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of our mission and business operations.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Workforce Modernization
drivers.description: Increased funding and manpower (1,678 FTEs) reflects the alignment of civilian staffing to validated mission requirements pursuant to Executive Order 14210, implementing the Presidents Department of Government Efficiency Workforce Optimization Initiative and the March 2025 Deputy Secretary of War memorandum. The Air Force conducted comprehensive data-hygiene and manpower- validation efforts, resulting in a correction where FY2026 staffing levels were set below the Base Support established requirements. The FY 2027 request reflects the full requirement necessary to support mission execution and workforce modernization. These FTEs support mission essential fire, Law Enforcement and emergency services; maintenance and logistics positions; nuclear enterprise support; Air Operations Centers support for Defense Planning Guidance (DPG) priority investments related to expansion, modernization, and diversification of our nuclear deterrent and prioritization of the readiness of forces for the Joint Force.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Average Workyear Cost Adjustment
drivers.description: Increased funding in Civilian Personnel compensation adjusts average workyear costs. Each year Air Force uses detailed execution and cost factor analysis to update civilian compensation costs for the purpose of accurately forecasting budget estimates for the civilian workforce. The Subactivity Group average cost adjustment is a result of these cost changes as well as updated pay raise, awards, and benefit assumptions.

drivers.title: Operational Communications - Enterprise Information Technology (EIT) Compute & Store
drivers.description: Funds support Oracle licenses, Enterprise Resource Planning Common Services (ERP-CS), and Cloud One requirements, addressing historical underfunding of Air Force EIT Compute/Store needs. The Oracle Enterprise Software License Agreement enables unlimited use of core Oracle products, critical security patches, and expert support for over 300 Department of the Air Force systems. ERP-CS provides essential cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, and application support for key DAF ERP systems (e.g. Defense Enterprise Accounting and Management System (DEAMS); Military Personnel Data System (MILPDS); and Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO)), serving as their foundation. Cloud One consolidates critical capabilities into a secure platform, supporting the Air Force Portal, warfighter applications, AI, data mesh, edge computing, and Zero Trust cybersecurity. This budget ensures Warfighters have the collaborative software and computing tools needed to sustain a ready and capable force.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Enhanced Performance Award Pool for DoW Civilian Employees
drivers.description: Increased funding strengthens the Department's ability to recognize and reward the civilian workforce whose expertise and continuity underpin mission success. Expanded award capacity helps retain the talent that sustains warfighter readiness, drives innovation, and ensures uninterrupted support across the enterprise. Investing in civilian recognition directly reinforces the workforce that delivers stability, operation excellence, and long-term capability for the Department.

drivers.title: Facilities Operations Support - US Indo-Pacific Command Yap International Airport, Wake Island
drivers.description: Program execution encountered delays and slipped from FY2025 to FY2026, funding reflects the one-time decrease after increase to support acquisition of land for an agreed upon defense site under appropriate international agreement required to complete the runway extension, parking apron, and taxiway construction at Yap International Airport, Wake Island.

drivers.description: Increases funds to support the active duty military end strength growth. Funding will be used to recruit additional Family Child Care (FCC) providers, allow for more non-traditional and specialized hourly programs, secure additional spaces for Military Child Care in Your Neighborhood (MCCYN), and provide incrementally increasing operational support. This increase is a programmatic investment to support active duty end strength growth and their accompanying families.

drivers.description: Decrease in funding following a one-time increase provided in P.L. 119-75 FY 2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act - Base Operations Support.

The Air Force conducted comprehensive data-hygiene and manpower-validation efforts, resulting in a correction where FY2026 staffing levels were set below the Airlift Operations Program established requirements. The FY2027 request reflects the full requirement necessary to provide the initial skills training and education essential to managing complex weapons systems. Additionally. this program provides the enhanced technical skills needed throughout a member's career to accomplish the Air Force's mission.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Enhanced Performance Award Pool for DoW Civilian Employees

Programmed funding levels will partially fund the operations occurring at six currently active Air Combat Command forward operating locations. This aligns with the National Defense Strategy to prioritize investments developing resilient, survivable systems and lethality in contested environments. The Air Force is taking risk in this program by not funding the resulting shortfall. drivers.title: Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) Combat Enhancement - Integrated Broadcast System
drivers.description: Increase for the transition of the Integrated Broadcast System (IBS) from procurement to sustainment. IBS provides warfighters with 24/7 near-real time threat warning, situational awareness, intelligence exploitation and information dissemination. Funding increase will provide engineering services and reach back support that includes in-plant engineering for sustainment of fielded equipment and on-site support for Theater and Geographic Interface Network Nodes. This increase also funds software and hardware technical refresh and support for the IBS Network Service communications architecture and brings the Operation and Maintenance funding to a steady state. Op32: 922 Equipment Maintenance by Contract 925 Equipment Purchases (Non-Fund)

drivers.title: Personnel Recovery - Guardian Angel Facilities
drivers.description: Increase for Guardian Angel squadron furniture, fixtures, and equipment for new facilities used to house pararescue men, combat rescue officers, Survival, Evasion, Resistance and Escape (SERE) specialists and thirteen other combat support Air Force Specialty Codes. Funding right-sizes the functionality required to accommodate mission growth and increasingly demanding operational wartime rescue. Op32: 925 Equipment Purchases (Non-Fund)

Reduces duplicative efforts since Allied/Partner Nations provide this capability. Op32: 101 Executive General Schedule

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - 9th Air Force Joint Task Force Headquarters
drivers.description: Increase provides full-year funding and manpower to Combat Enhancement Forces (Subactivity Group 11C, +1,168, 9 FTEs) in support of Air Force led, deployable Joint Task Force (JTF) headquarters. Civilian personnel provide command and control for this mission as directed by the Chief of Staff of the Air Force, and allows the JTF headquarters to achieve operational readiness as a Global Response Force capable headquarters. Op32: 101 Executive General Schedule

drivers.title: Readiness Training - Reforge Proof of Concept
drivers.description: Increase reflects one-time plus up to fund a study for a proof of concept supporting the Commander, Air Combat Command initiative to "Rebuild the Forge". The study will provide cost estimates for a long-term program and reduce uncertainty of affordability to the Air Force. The proof of concept will use six evolutions to deliberately develop improved methods and capabilities for rebuilding current fighter pilot training into a proficiency-based, alternate/virtual reality integrated, initial tactical training mechanism for fighter production and development. Combat Air Forces has a critical shortage of experienced pilots. This concept of operations uses advanced trainers to teach initial tactical skills in twelve months prior to arrival at the Flight Training Unit. It is projected to reduce training days by fifty percent and replenish the experienced fighter pilot shortage by 2030. Op32: 925 Equipment Purchases (Non-Fund)

drivers.title: Readiness Training - Simulators Common Architecture Requirements and Standards
drivers.description: Decrease to Simulators Common Architecture Requirements and Standards (SCARS) Operation and Maintenance funding to address capability gaps associated with the Joint TACAIR Synthesis Training initiative, which interfaces with SCARS to improve high- end advanced training capability in the synthetic training environment. Remaining Operation and Maintenance funding provides cyber-security monitoring, threat detection, critical software patching, critical common training environment models required to achieve full-spectrum readiness and lower sustainment costs for the Air Force operational training infrastructure. This activity supports improved interoperability and data sharing. Op32: 922 Equipment Maintenance by Contract

drivers.title: Readiness Exercises - Travel
drivers.description: Increase is necessary to support mission-critical operational travel post pandemic to achieve the minimum-sustainable requirement. Op32: 308 Travel of Persons

drivers.title: Readiness Training - Readiness Tools for Lethality
drivers.description: Increase provides for technical and analytical support, and sustainment of readiness reporting applications used to provide decision- level data to Combatant Commanders, the Joint Chiefs of Staff, and other key users. The support and tools will be used to evaluate the readiness and capability of the United States Armed Forces to carry out assigned and potential missions/tasks. Funding enables mission readiness assessments against standardized missions and tasks. Applications and training suites included are Defense Readiness Reporting System (DRRS) and Defense Property Accountability System (DPAS). Op32: 922 Equipment Maintenance by Contract 933 Studies, Analysis, and Evaluations
