drivers.title: Nuclear Deterrence Combat Forces - Modernization and Sustainment
drivers.description: Increase funds to provide engineering analysis, test evaluation, and programmatic surveillance and sustainment support for nuclear integration and certification of the B61-12 munition. This funds Air Force Nuclear Weapons Center (AFNWC) to contract Johns Hopkins University (JHU) Lab to develop a B61-12 TKA reliability model, which is a critical enabler for nuclear weapon training, certification, and preparation for Initial Nuclear Surety Inspection.

drivers.title: Disaster Relief Supplemental
drivers.description: Decrease funding for the one-time FY 2025 add from P.L. 118-58 Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2025.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - B-1 Divestment Restoral
drivers.description: Increase full-year funding and manpower to (22 FTEs) to provide restoration of the B-1 inventory. Additional manpower will support the multi-mission, supersonic bomber restoration to increase the number of fully operational B-1s. Manpower will assist in restoring safe and sustained aircraft back into the fleet of long range bombing force.

drivers.title: Transfer from Discretionary to Mandatory
drivers.description: Decrease in Primary Combat Forces and Support funding will be appropriately offset by funding sourced from the Reconciliation Bill (H.R.1) upon enactment.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - F-35 Operational Beddown
drivers.description: Increase half-year funding and manpower to (32 FTEs) to provide the necessary funding and manpower to accomplish F-35 disconnects and operational bed down requirements. Funds Ops bed downs at Tyndall and Misawa, F-35 MILCON, F-35 DT jet sustainment and flying hours, depot repair capacity, MX Trainers, Full Mission Simulators, LO Verification, ALIS to ODIN Transition, Engine sustainment, and ACE ABDR.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Collaborative Combat Aircraft Manpower
drivers.description: Increase full-year funding and manpower (4 FTEs) in support of the Collaborative Combat Aircraft program. Additional manpower will analyze the autonomy, mission systems, and air vehicle developments required to expand the air dominance of uncrewed aircraft.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - B-2 Restoration
drivers.description: Increase full-year funding and manpower to (3 FTEs) to provide restoration of aircraft in the B-2 inventory. Additional manpower will support the global delivery and deterrence multi-role bomber mission.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - F16 Restoration
drivers.description: Increase half-year funding and manpower (2 FTEs) to provide partial restoration of the F-16 inventory at Eielson Air Force Base. Manpower will support the primary combat mission of providing aerospace control for homeland defense missions in the Alaska Theater of Operations.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Weapons Generation Facility Completion
drivers.description: Increase full-year funding and manpower (1 FTE) to support the implementation of Weapons Generation Facilities which consolidate weapons storage, maintenance, and training into one building. Functions of the additional manpower include security forces and maintenance needed to complete the construction which will subsequently ensure safe storage of the nuclear arsenal.

drivers.description: Increase supports Joint Simulation Environment (JSE) enhancements. Reinforces development and sustainment of JSE assets and environments addressing significant limitations in current weapon testing and training infrastructure. System supports four critical functions: integrated development and testing, tactics development, advance training, and systems experimentation.

drivers.title: Electronic Warfare - Electromagnetic Spectrum
drivers.description: Increase supports the acceleration of the Air Force Electromagnetic Spectrum operational capabilities by developing and deploying advanced electronic warfare (EW) techniques and infrastructure to counter emerging threats. This effort involves creating platform- agnostic development tools, modernizing EW systems, and enhancing capabilities to achieve spectrum superiority, particularly for 5th and next-generation aircraft, to stay ahead of adversaries and maintain dominance.

drivers.title: Special Operations Forces - Special Operations Wing Beddown at Davis-Monthan
drivers.description: Increase supports Secretary of the Air Force (SECAF) basing action for establishment of the 492d Special Operations Wing (SOW) at Davis-Monthan AFB, AZ. Provides funding (+$10,020) for temporary facility leases for 492 SOW HQ (existing facility renovation to be completed in FY 2028), MC-130J Special Operations Aircraft Maintenance Squadron (SOAMXS) (construction to be completed in FY 2028), and temporary Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIFs). Additionally, increase provides funding (+$6,850) for Furniture, Fixtures, and Equipment (FF&E) to outfit funded projects (MC-130J Squadron Operations, 492 Special Operations Theater Air Operations Squadron (SOTAOS), MC-130J simulator facility) as well as a readiness spares package mezzanine, classified vault, and weapons vault storage aides.

drivers.title: Special Operations Forces - Air Force Special Warfare Tactical Air Control Party
drivers.description: Increase supports the training and development of Air Force Special Warfare Tactical Air Control Party (TACP) personnel, enabling them to integrate and coordinate various combat assets, including air, ground, and naval firepower, electronic warfare, and medical evacuations. This integration allows TACP teams to bring synchronized and lethal firepower to the battlefield, enhancing the effectiveness of ground operations and supporting the success of special warfare missions.

drivers.title: ISR Combat Enhancement - 55th Wing Flood Recovery
drivers.description: Increase supports Military Construction (MILCON) fit-out of Furniture, Fixtures, and Equipment (FF&E) for flood recovery at the 55th Wing at Offutt AFB, NE.

drivers.title: Electronic Warfare - Information Warfare Training and Research Environment
drivers.description: Increase supports additional operational funding for the Department of the Air Force's Information Warfare Training and Research Environment (IWTRE) site, which is a unique facility that supports the development and experimentation of cross-cutting Information Warfare (IW) capabilities. The IWTRE site enables the Air Force to build and test integrated IW capabilities in a realistic and reactive environment, preparing them to compete against peer adversaries and achieve strategic objectives.

drivers.title: Combat Communications - Air Force Force Generation
drivers.description: Increase supports Air Force Force Generation (AFFORGEN) by enhancing its Agile Combat Employment (ACE) concept, providing 5th generation fighter units with advanced, scalable technologies to improve organic Command and Control (C2) capabilities. This upgrade allows Airmen to operate effectively in deployed or austere locations, similar to their home stations, with seamless integration across various networks. The initiative aims to increase lead wing capacity and reduce pre-deployment preparation time, ultimately strengthening the Air Force's ability to succeed in competitions or conflicts, particularly in the Indo-Pacific region. By doing so, it will improve training and enhance operational capabilities to counter pacing adversaries.

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs - Operation Inherent Resolve (OIR) - Efficiency - Contract Services
drivers.description: Reduces contracts for Advisory and Assistance Services to promote efficiencies and advance the policies of the Administration in alignment with Executive Order 14222, “Implementing the President’s Department of Government Efficiency Cost Efficiency Initiative.”

drivers.description: Increase full-year funding and personnel (22 FTEs) in response to strategic shift towards increased enterprise readiness. The added manpower ensures that crisis response and enterprise readiness can all execute concurrently. Manpower will execute and employ crisis response tasks which will enable military assets to focus on readiness.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Decelerate USAF Reoptimization
drivers.description: Decrease full-year funding and manpower for (22 FTEs) from the Air Force to decelerate re-optimization efforts but continue the lines of effort associated with standing up the Integrated Capabilities Command and six deployable air wings.

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs - Operation Inherent Resolve (OIR)
drivers.description: Decrease funds for ISR Combat Enhancement requirements in support of Operation Inherent Resolve (OIR).

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - MQ-9 Combat Line Allocations
drivers.description: Increase half-year funding and manpower (13 FTEs) to provide additional MQ-9 combat lines to the Global Force Management Allocation Plan (GFMAP). The GFMAP allocates and temporarily redistributes forces amongst Combatant Commands and meets emergent operational needs across the areas of responsibility.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Tactical Air Control Party Career Field Reduction
drivers.description: Decrease full-year funding and manpower from Combat Enhancement Forces (Subactivity Group 11C, -$780, -6 FTEs) to reduce the Tactical Air Control Party career field by 50 percent. This action reflects the Department of Defense's shift in focus to the modern pacing challenge. The Air Force will divest its manning and resources away from this close air support specialty.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Security Assistance - Misaligned Programs
drivers.description: Decrease full-year funding and manpower (3 FTEs) from the Air Force to eliminate the Aviation Leadership Program, Inter-European Air Forces Academy, and USAFE/AFAFRICA's Combat Training School; and to eliminate programs proposed by the Air Force to meet DoD overall funding reductions. The eliminations the Air Force proposed include: - Eliminate 571st Mobility Support Advisory Squadron - Eliminate 818th Mobility Support Advisory Squadron - Eliminate 637th International Support Squadron - Eliminate USAFE/AFAFRICA's 4th Combat Training Squadron.

drivers.title: Readiness Training - Adversary Air (ADAIR)
drivers.description: Increase supports the Combat Air Forces (CAF) Contracted Air Support (CAS) program by accelerating the ramp to phase-out of Adversary Air (ADAIR) training contract. The Combat Air Forces (CAF) Contracted Air Support (CAS) program is adapting to meet the evolving needs of the Air Force and ensure effective training for its personnel program provides realistic adversary air threats to train pilots and Joint Terminal Attack Controllers (JTACs). The CAS program supports pilot production and post-graduate operational training, ultimately contributing to the Air Force's training objectives and utilizes contracted support services to aid in pilot training at Flying Training Units (FTUs) and benefits pilot combat readiness.

drivers.title: Readiness Exercises - Air Task Force (ATF) PACAF
drivers.description: Increase supports enhanced integration of Air Task Force (ATF) into Pacific Air Forces (PACAF) theater exercises, which includes mission tasking’s from Air Force Special Operations Command (AFSOC) and Air Force Global Strike Command (AFGSC). This support also facilitates the movement of personnel and equipment, ensuring seamless operations. Additionally, it provides a training pipeline for Joint Terminal Attack Controllers to develop and refine their critical skills, preparing them for high-stakes operations.

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs - Other Theater Requirements and Related Missions
drivers.description: Increase funds for Readiness Exercises and Training requirements in support of Other Theater missions.

In this Subactivity Group, funds operational readiness exercises to include logistics, essential equipment, SAAM airlift and deployment travel expenses associated with the broader increased tempo and mission requirements in priority theaters.

drivers.title: Readiness Exercises - Pacific Air Forces Exercises
drivers.description: Decrease following a previous increase for Pacific Air Forces (PACAF) Exercises that supported a surge for high-quality 4th/5th Generation exercise capacity. Provided critical Agile Combat Employment (ACE) training opportunities to obtain/maintain operational capability. Decrease reflects Air Force priorities and decisions to accept risk regarding Indo-Pacific Command (INDOPACOM) readiness/emphasis on building partnership capacity.

drivers.description: Increase supports Joint Simulation Environment (JSE) operational . Reinforces sustainment of JSE assets and environments addressing significant limitations in current weapon testing and training infrastructure. System supports four critical functions: integrated development and testing, tactics development, advance training, and systems experimentation.

drivers.description: Increase funds for Readiness Exercises in support of Operation Enduring Sentinel (OES). This supports the five air bases in the USCENTCOM area of responsibility and aligns to the current theater requirements.

drivers.description: Decrease full-year funding and manpower from (3 FTEs) to programmatically adjust restored manpower from F-16 fighter squadrons.

The eliminations the Air Force proposed include: - Eliminate 571st Mobility Support Advisory Squadron - Eliminate 818th Mobility Support Advisory Squadron - Eliminate 637th International Support Squadron - Eliminate USAFE/AFAFRICA's 4th Combat Training Squadron.

drivers.title: Transfer from Discretionary to Mandatory
drivers.description: Decrease in Depot Purchase Equipment Maintenance funding will be appropriately offset by funding sourced from the Reconciliation Bill (H.R.1) upon enactment.

drivers.title: Rapid Global Mobility - KC-135
drivers.description: Increase for the KC-135 Stratotanker is critical to sustaining the Air Force's core air refueling capacity as the service transitions to a mixed-fleet posture. This increase provides essential funding for an expanded Programmed Depot Maintenance (PDM) program to address increased aircraft age and maintenance demands. Operational demands for supporting overseas operations are impacting engine and Contractor Logistics Support (CLS). These funds are essential to maintaining the KC-135's high operational tempo, ensuring global reach and power projection for the Joint Force.

drivers.title: Global Precision Attack - B-52
drivers.description: Increase for the B-52 Stratofortress is critical to sustain the long-term readiness of this vital bomber, ensuring its continued viability as a key element of the U.S. nuclear triad and conventional strike force. Despite its age, the B-52's relevance has only increased in recent years, leading to higher operational demands and accelerating fatigue on critical components like engines and airframes. Increased funding will address critical sustainment needs, including engine overhauls, structural repairs, and modernization of avionics and communication systems. This investment is essential to maintaining the B-52's ability to deliver global strike capabilities and provide a credible deterrent until the B-21 Raider can be fully fielded.

drivers.title: Air Superiority - F-22A
drivers.description: Increase for the F-22 Raptor is required to address escalating maintenance demands. This reflects an increase in depot level maintenance hours needed for individual parts, assemblies, or subassemblies based on historical data and increased operational and software sustainment requirements to counter aging vulnerabilities. The F-22 program will also see growth in engines, contractor logistics support management, and sustaining engineering, congruent with increased use. This funding increase significantly enhances F-22 pilot production by ensuring the availability of serviceable aircraft.

drivers.title: In-Canal Active Hearing Protection
drivers.description: Decrease following a one-time FY 2025 Congressional mark increase to provide funding support for critical in-canal active hearing protection.

drivers.title: Rapid Global Mobility - AC-130J
drivers.description: Increase for the AC-130J Ghostrider, which provides ground forces with an unparalleled expeditionary, direct-fire platform, delivering precise firepower and persistent air support to special operations forces. Recent deployments have demonstrated the AC-130J's effectiveness in urban operations and denied territories, exceeding mission requirements for close air support, air interdiction, and armed reconnaissance. To sustain this critical capability, increased funding is vital to support the growing demand for AC-130J engine overhauls and Contractor Logistics Support, driven by higher operational tempos and the transition to the Rolls-Royce propulsion contract. This investment will ensure the long-term health of the AC-130J fleet, enabling the platform to deliver decisive airpower in support of special operations forces for years to come.

drivers.title: Global Precision Attack - F-35
drivers.description: Increase for the F-35 program is driven by escalating sustainment demands across the growing aircraft inventory. Specifically, depot level reparables requirements have increased to meet higher operational tempos across the fleet. This increase also funds growth in software and laboratory sustainment demands, driven by the evolving threat environment. These investments are essential to maintaining the F-35's technological advantage and ensuring its continued contribution to global precision attack.

drivers.title: Global Integrated Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance - MQ-9 UAV
drivers.description: Increase for the MQ-9 Reaper, a remotely piloted aircraft providing a unique capability to perform strike, coordination, and reconnaissance against high-level targets. This increase funds the procurement of additional Multi-Spectral Targeting System-B (MTS-B) sensor pods, enhancing the MQ-9’s ability to find, fix, and track time-sensitive targets. This investment is projected to increase the number of combat lines available for tasking by combatant commanders. This ultimately enables the MQ-9 to better the increasing demand for its intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance capabilities in support of global operations. OP:32 661: AF Consolidated Sustainment 931 Other Depot Maintenance (Non-DWCF)

drivers.title: Rapid Global Mobility - MC-130J
drivers.description: Increase for the MC-130J Commando II. This increase supports the modernization and sustainment of the MC-130J fleet, which has experienced increased operational demands in recent years. This funding ensures these aircraft have the advanced capabilities necessary to operate in contested environments. This directly enhances the readiness of special operations forces, allowing them to conduct critical missions such as infiltration, exfiltration, and resupply in hostile territory.

drivers.title: Undergraduate Pilot Training
drivers.description: Increase for the T-6 Texan II & T-38 Talon, the primary trainer for USAF student pilots, is critical to meet the escalating demands for pilot production. This increase supports 6 additional T-6 Aircraft Consolidation Induction aircraft, exceeding planned capacity to ensure sufficient aircraft are available to meet projected future training requirements. As well as structural upgrades and service life extension modifications to address aging-related issues and extend the T-38's operational lifespan. This effort directly supports the fielding a more lethal and ready force for the US and allied partners, by providing a steady flow of new pilots trained to the highest standards. These additional aircraft will be sustained through depot-level heavy maintenance and sustainment engineering, ensuring their continued availability and extending their service life.

drivers.title: Nuclear Deterrence Operations - B-2
drivers.description: Increase for the B-2 Spirit is essential to maintain the readiness and effectiveness of this critical strategic asset, ensuring its ability to penetrate enemy defenses and deliver both conventional and nuclear munitions. As the B-2 fleet ages, the need for enhanced sustainment, modernization, and software upgrades has intensified to counter evolving threats and maintain its low-observable characteristics. Increased funding will address critical maintenance backlogs, support the timely replacement of aging components, and enable the integration of advanced technologies that enhance the B-2's survivability and lethality. This investment is vital to preserving the B-2's unique capabilities as a cornerstone of the U.S. nuclear triad and a guarantor of global strategic stability.

drivers.title: Transfer from Discretionary to Mandatory
drivers.description: Decrease in Real Property Maintenance, Facilities Sustainment funding will be appropriately offset by funding sourced from the Reconciliation Bill (H.R.1) upon enactment.

drivers.title: Facilities Restoration and Modernization - Maintain FSRM at 1.5% PRV
drivers.description: Increase in funding to execute targeted restoration and modernization of failed or failing critical infrastructure, improving the overall condition of the Department's facility inventory. Funding level will maintain the Maintenance and Repair ratio at 1.5 percent of plant replacement value (PRV), holding the minimal gap to the required amount of funding per the Infrastructure Investment Action Plan (I2AP) to properly maintain and sustain Air Force infrastructure in accordance with the Consolidated Budget Review Guidance and consistent with the Department of Defense's focus on funding FSRM. This program increase is net of the effect of the decreases driven by one-time cost increases to FY 2025 budget requests for B-21 Facilities and Davis-Monthan Basing Action.

drivers.title: Disaster Relief Supplemental
drivers.description: Decrease funding for the one-time FY 2025 add from P.L. 118-58 Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2025.

drivers.title: Facilities Restoration and Modernization - Unaccompanied Housing Improvements
drivers.description: Increase in Unaccompanied Housing (UH) funding levels to provide continued support to the highest priority requirements. Improvements will target heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC), electrical and plumbing systems, and overall restoration and modernization projects to improve housing facilities in poor or failing conditions.

drivers.title: Facilities Restoration and Modernization - Unit of Action Initial Standup
drivers.description: Increase to support initial standup and sustainment of Air Operational Wings as mission ready "units of action" categorized as Deployable Combat Wings (DCW), In-Place Combat Wings (ICW) or Combat Generation Wings (CGW). Each will have its own structure, with a redesigned concept of support for Agile Combat Employment (ACE), to ensure the wings are prepared to execute their missions with assigned Airmen and units. This increase will also establish the relationship between Combat Wings, which will focus on mission-level warfighting readiness, and Base Commands, which will focus on supporting Combat Wings and operating the base in competition, crisis, and conflict.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Efficiency - Workforce Optimization
drivers.description: Decrease funding and manpower (443 FTEs) to optimize the workforce in compliance with Executive Order 14210, "Implementing the President's Department of Government Efficiency Workforce Optimization Initiative."

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Average Workyear Cost Adjustment
drivers.description: Increase funding in Civilian Personnel compensation adjusts average workyear costs. Each year, the Air Force uses detailed execution and cost factor analysis to realign and update civilian compensation costs and manpower for the purpose of accurately forecasting budget estimates for the civilian workforce. The Subactivity Group average cost adjustment is a result of these changes as well as updated pay raise, awards, and benefit assumptions.

drivers.title: Facilities Restoration and Modernization - Classified
drivers.description: Increase to classified program. Details will be provided under separate cover with the Classified Operation and Maintenance justification materials.

drivers.title: Facilities Restoration and Modernization - Support Equipment Electrification
drivers.description: Increase in funds required to procure electric equipment, chargers, and upgrades to support the modernization of electrical infrastructure for six depot maintenance locations.

drivers.title: Facilities Restoration and Modernization - Enhancements for Future Pilot Training Sites
drivers.description: Decrease following a one-time programmatic increase to provide additional funding to support site enhancements at Ebbing Field for future joint pilot trainings.

drivers.title: Facilities Sustainment - Arctic FSRM Support
drivers.description: Decrease following a one-time programmatic increase to provide additional funding support for critical facilities sustainment projects in the Arctic.

drivers.title: Facilities Restoration and Modernization - Child Development Center (CDC) Support
drivers.description: One-time increase in funds provides for restoration and modernization of CDC facilities currently in poor condition to best provide Service members with affordable and quality childcare which is critical to the mission readiness.

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs - Other Theater Requirements and Related Missions
drivers.description: Increase funds for facility sustainment requirements in support of Other Theater Requirements.

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs - Operation Enduring Sentinel (OES)
drivers.description: Decrease funds for facility sustainment and base support requirements in support of Operation Enduring Sentinel (OES). This supports the five air bases in the USCENTCOM area of responsibility and aligns to the current theater requirements.

drivers.title: Efficiency - Travel
drivers.description: Reduces discretionary travel funding to align with Executive Order 14222, “Implementing the President’s Department of Government Efficiency Cost Efficiency Initiative.”

drivers.title: Cyberspace Superiority - Distributed Cyber Warfare Operations
drivers.description: Decrease for AF Cyber Offensive reflects a strategic realignment of resources within the Air Force, prioritizing the modernization of core cyber infrastructure and defensive capabilities in response to evolving budgetary constraints. While maintaining a credible cyber offense remains important, the Air Force will leverage existing tools and partnerships to mitigate any potential risk associated with this budget reduction. This strategic shift allows for increased investment in fortifying cyber defenses, enhancing network security, and developing innovative solutions to counter emerging cyber threats. The Air Force remains committed to maintaining a credible deterrent against malicious cyber actors and will continue to conduct offensive cyber operations as required to support national security objectives. Cyberspace Superiority is a degree of dominance in cyberspace by one force that permits the secure, reliable conduct of operations at a given time and place without prohibitive interference.

drivers.title: Cyberspace Superiority - Air Force Cyber Defense
drivers.description: Increase for AF Cyber Command and Control to bolster the resilience and adaptability of critical command and control systems against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats. The increase continues efforts from the FY 2025 congressional add to repair or replace hardware for sustaining engineering software requirements. As adversaries continue to develop and deploy advanced cyber weapons, the need for robust cybersecurity measures and rapid system upgrades has intensified. The Air Force Cyberspace Defense weapon system coordinates and executes resources needed to assess, analyze, and respond to network security incidents, intrusive activity, vulnerabilities, malicious logic, or viruses. Increased funding will allow for enhanced software development and sustainment of the Cyber Command and Control Mission System (C3MS), ensuring its ability to operate effectively in contested cyberspace. The system provides constant monitoring and defense of the Department's Non-Secure Internet Protocol Router (NIPR)/Secret Internet Protocol Router (SIPR) computer networks against hostile attack. This funding directly supports the warfighter by providing uninterrupted command and control capabilities, enabling decisive action in a dynamic and evolving threat environment.

drivers.title: Cyberspace Superiority - Air Force Intranet Control
drivers.description: Decrease for AF Cyber Operations reflects a strategic realignment of resources within the Air Force, prioritizing the modernization of critical cyber infrastructure and development of cutting-edge cyber capabilities. Decreases the licensing costs, subscription services, and support renewals for fielded software and firmware operating within the Air Force Intranet Control weapon system. The Intranet Control is a critical part of the mission to generate, project, and sustain combat cyberspace power by defending and shaping the cyberspace terrain. While maintaining a robust cyber defense posture remains a top priority, the Air Force will leverage existing resources and pursue innovative solutions to mitigate any potential risks associated with this budget reduction. This strategic shift allows for increased investment in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and other advanced technologies essential for countering sophisticated cyber threats in the future. The Air Force remains committed to defending its networks, deterring malicious cyber activity, and ensuring freedom of maneuver within the cyber domain, even in a resource-constrained environment

drivers.title: Transfer from Discretionary to Mandatory
drivers.description: Decrease in Contractor Logistics Support and System Support funding will be appropriately offset by funding sourced from the Reconciliation Bill (H.R.1) upon enactment.

drivers.title: Global Integrated Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance - U-2
drivers.description: Decrease for U-2 Systems reduces funding for planned sensor upgrades and modernization efforts, impacting the platform's long- term intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities. This budgetary constraint slows the pace of technological advancements for engines & sustaining engineering needed to maintain the U-2’s edge in contested airspace and counter evolving threats. While yielding immediate cost savings, this decrease creates risk by potentially degrading the quality and timeliness of intelligence gathered by the U-2. Ultimately, this constraint could hinder the warfighter's situational awareness and decision-making capabilities in future operations.

drivers.title: Nuclear Deterrence - ICBM
drivers.description: Decrease for Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM) Minuteman III reflects reduced reliance on legacy systems in favor of modernization efforts. This decrease defers upgrades to the Little Mountain Test Facility (LMTF) and Strategic Missile Integration Complex (SMIC), prioritizing immediate readiness over long-term sustainment of aging infrastructure.

drivers.title: Air Superiority - F-22
drivers.description: Increase for the F-22 Raptor is required to address escalating maintenance demands to strip and reapply reversion-prone low observable coatings. This reflects an increase in depot level maintenance hours needed for individual parts, assemblies, or subassemblies based on historical data and increased operational requirements. The F-22 program will also see growth in engines, contractor logistics support management, and sustaining engineering, congruent with increased use. This funding increase significantly enhances F-22 pilot production by ensuring the availability of serviceable aircraft.

drivers.title: Rapid Global Mobility - C-17
drivers.description: Decrease for the C-17 Globemaster III reflects necessary budgetary constraints, impacting the strategic airlift fleet's planned maintenance and sustainment activities. While the C-17 remains crucial for projecting and sustaining military forces globally, this decrease will reduce the acquisition of spare engines and components, potentially impacting aircraft availability rates. The long-term effects of these reductions on the Air Force's ability to meet global airlift requirements will be closely monitored. Mitigation strategies, including prioritizing maintenance for the most critical components, will be implemented to minimize risk and maintain the C-17's operational effectiveness within a constrained fiscal environment.

drivers.title: Rapid Global Mobility - C-130J
drivers.description: Program Decrease for the C-130J Super Hercules reflects necessary budgetary constraints, requiring a reduction in planned depot- level maintenance for this essential tactical airlifter. While the C-130J remains crucial for delivering troops and equipment to austere locations, this decrease defers some scheduled maintenance actions, increasing the risk of reduced aircraft availability and potentially impacting operational readiness. The impact of these reductions on the Air Force's ability to meet global airlift requirements will be closely monitored, and risk mitigation measures will be explored to maintain the C-130J's operational effectiveness within a constrained budget environment.

drivers.title: Command and Control - E-4B NAOC
drivers.description: Increase for the E-4B National Military Command System is essential to mitigate growing risks associated with system obsolescence and ensure this critical platform's continued survivability and mission effectiveness. As a key component of the National Military Command System, the E-4B provides a vital command, control, and communications center for national leadership in times of crisis. This funding increase will prioritize essential technical refreshes, address critical Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages (DMSMS) issues, and support necessary upgrades to the E-4B's aging communication systems. These investments are essential to guarantee the E-4B can continue fulfilling its critical national security role throughout its remaining service life.

drivers.title: Rapid Global Mobility - KC-46A
drivers.description: Increase for the KC-46A Pegasus to provide essential funding for modernization and sustainment efforts to maintain the survivability of the fleet. These aircraft flew an increased number of missions last year, highlighting their capability for global reach through aerial refueling operations. This investment ensures the KC-46A can continue to support the Air Force's Rapid Global Mobility mission, delivering fuel and extending the reach of U.S. and allied aircraft around the world.

drivers.title: Rapid Global Mobility - CV-22
drivers.description: Increase for the CV-22 Osprey, a unique tilt-rotor aircraft providing long-range infiltration, exfiltration, and resupply for special operations forces, is crucial due to escalating maintenance requirements driven by increased global operational demands. This increase directly enhances mission readiness by funding additional Programmed Depot Maintenance (PDM) cycles for the CV-22 fleet. These intensive maintenance actions, conducted approximately every four years per aircraft, are essential to sustaining the Osprey's complex systems and ensuring its continued availability for critical special operations missions. This investment is essential to maintaining the CV-22's critical role in global special operations, upholding its position as a premier platform for long-range insertion and extraction in high-threat environments.

drivers.title: Global Precision Attack - F-16
drivers.description: Increase for the F-16 Fighting Falcon to support the continued modernization and sustainment of the F-16, a critical multi-role fighter comprising nearly half of the USAF fighter force. Due to increased global commitments and the aircraft's expanding role in operations like Inherent Resolve and Freedom's Sentinel, demand for F-16 maintenance and modernization has escalated. This increase provides essential funding for upgrades, structural repairs, and software enhancements, ultimately bolstering the F-16's combat readiness and ensuring its continued viability as a cornerstone of the U.S. Air Force's air power.

drivers.title: EURO-NATO Joint Jet Pilot Training
drivers.description: Increase for the T-6 Texan II & T-38 Talon, the primary trainers for EURO-NATO student pilots, is critical to meet the escalating demands for pilot production. This increase supports 6 additional T-6 Aircraft Consolidation Induction aircraft, exceeding planned capacity to ensure sufficient aircraft are available to meet projected future training requirements. Also includes structural upgrades and service life extension modifications to address aging-related issues and extend the T-38's operational lifespan. This effort directly supports the fielding a more lethal and ready force for the U.S. and allied partners, by providing a steady flow of new pilots trained to the highest standards. These additional aircraft will be sustained through depot-level heavy maintenance and sustainment engineering, ensuring their continued availability and extending their service life.

drivers.title: Global Precision Attack - Tactical Air Control Party
drivers.description: Increase for the Tactical Air Control Party-Modernization (TACP-M) program is critical to enhancing the close air support (CAS) capabilities of TACP units. This increase provides essential funding for replacing obsolete and outdated communication equipment within the TACP Family of Systems (FoS), which has reached the end of its service life. This modernization effort directly enhances the warfighter's ability to effectively coordinate and de-conflict CAS missions, improving the precision and responsiveness of airpower in support of ground operations. Ultimately, this investment reduces the risk of fratricide and strengthens the overall effectiveness of joint combat operations.

drivers.title: Global Integrated Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance - RC-135
drivers.description: Increase for the RC-135V/W Rivet Joint, a reconnaissance aircraft that provides near real-time intelligence collection, analysis, and dissemination capabilities. This increase funds the accelerated modernization of the Rivet Joint fleet's communication and sensor suites, enhancing its ability to detect, identify, and geolocate signals. This investment improves the aircraft's intelligence-gathering capabilities against increasingly sophisticated adversary threats. Ultimately, this initiative ensures the RC-135 remains a vital asset for providing actionable intelligence to theater and national-level commanders in support of global operations.

drivers.title: Nuclear Deterrence Operations - MILSATCOM Terminals
drivers.description: Increase for MILSATCOM NC3 Terminals to support the modernization of aging terminals and the acquisition of advanced capabilities to maintain a resilient and secure communication network. These terminals have experienced a significant increase in demand for data transmission and voice communication across all combatant commands. This investment is critical to ensuring reliable connectivity for critical Nuclear Command and Communications (NC3) functions, directly supporting the President, Secretary of Defense, and military leaders in executing national security directives.

drivers.title: Air Superiority - Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missile (JASSM)
drivers.description: Increase for the Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missile (JASSM) program supports the Air Force's global precision strike mission. This increase is necessary to enhance the missile's capabilities against evolving threats and to maintain its critical standoff range, which directly improves aircrew survivability and mission success.

drivers.title: Command and Control - Wide Area Surveillance (WAS)
drivers.description: Increase for Wide Area Surveillance (WAS) is critical to enhancing the defense of the National Capitol Region against evolving airborne threats. This increase supports the continued fielding and sustainment of advanced air defense sensors, exceeding prior year levels to expand coverage and enhance early warning capabilities. This expansion of WAS sensor deployment directly benefits NORAD's Homeland Defense mission by providing real-time tracking data on low, slow, and asymmetrical threats, strengthening the overall air picture. This investment ensures timely and accurate information is relayed to Air Defense Sectors, enabling more effective threat response and safeguarding critical national assets.

drivers.title: Rapid Global Mobility - KC-135s
drivers.description: Increase for the KC-135 Stratotanker is critical to sustaining the Air Force's core air refueling capacity as the service transitions to a mixed-fleet posture. This increase provides essential funding for an expanded Programmed Depot Maintenance (PDM) program to address increased aircraft age and maintenance demands. These investments are essential to maintaining the KC-135's high operational tempo, ensuring global reach and power projection for the Joint Force.

drivers.title: Combat Air Forces
drivers.description: Program increase to the Combat Air Forces (CAF) flying hour program provides critical support to air forces in direct combat operations. This includes a range of mission sets such as fighter, bomber, command and control, combat search and rescue, and intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance aircraft, ultimately enhancing their ability to execute diverse missions and protect national interests. Despite a reduction in flying hours, CAF has experienced a funding increase, driven by the elevated operational tempo of advanced weapons systems, as well as rising cost per flying hour rates attributed to increased consumption of fuel, aircraft parts, and supplies. The net result is a decrease of (-36,724) flying hours. The following details by aircraft type provides insight into the platforms contributing to reduction in flying hours, as well as the resulting change in funding levels from the increased utilization of higher-cost weapon systems. The following aircraft have reductions in flying hours: A-10C by (-24,053 hours), B-1B (-66 hours), B-52H (-9 hours), E-11A (-1,206 hours), E-3G (-3,142 hours), EC-130H (-673 hours), F-15C (-799 hours), F-15D (-273 hours), F-15E (-8,680 hours), F-16C (-1,900 hours), F-16D (-411 hours), HC-130J (-1,794 hours), HH-60G (-1,422 hours), and the RC-135U by (-135 hours). In contrast, the F-15EX increased by (9,362 hours), F-22A (3,820 hours), F-35A (3,790 hours), B-2A (752 hours), and the HH-60W by (477 hours). The following aircraft had no changes: E-4B, E-9A, RC-135S, RC-135V, RC-135W, T-38A, TC-135W, and WC-135C. Net adjustments in dollars may not always follow in the direction of the hour change due to price and consumption adjustments in the cost per flying hour rates for fuel, aircraft parts and supplies.

drivers.title: Mobility Air Forces
drivers.description: Program decrease for the Mobility Air Forces (MAF) flying hours program, which provides critical support to air forces delivering airlift, air refueling, special air missions, and aeromedical evacuations. This reduction is primarily driven by a decrease of (-13,391) flying hours, coupled with lower hourly costs associated with MAF weapon systems. The following details by aircraft type provides insight into the platforms contributing to the reduction in flying hours. The following aircraft have reductions in flying hours: KC-135R by (-5,934 hours), UH-1N (-4,694 hours), C-40B (-1,101 hours), C- 21A (-920 hours), KC-135T (-909 hours), C-12J (-735 hours), EC-37B (-400 hours), C-37A (-361 hours), C-12F (-282 hours), C-130J (-270 hours), C-5M (-142 hours), and the KC-46A by (-33 hours). In contrast, the C-40C increased by (140 hours), MH-139A (1,935 hours), and the C-17A (173 hours). The following aircraft had no changes: KC-10A, C-37B, C-32A, and the VC-25A. Net adjustments in dollars may not always follow in the direction of the hour change due to price and consumption adjustments in the cost per flying hour for fuel, parts and supplies.

drivers.title: Formal Training
drivers.description: Program increase to the Formal Training program utilizes flying hours to facilitate the development of initial flying skills and aircrew production, ultimately enhancing the operational readiness of our aircrews. Despite the reduction in flying hours to executable levels, the program has experienced a funding increase. This is primarily attributed to the elevated operational tempo of advanced trainer weapon systems, as well as rising cost per flying hour rates, which is driven by increased consumption of fuel, aircraft parts, and supplies. To ensure alignment with executable levels, the program has implemented a reduction of (-40,954) flight hours. The following details by aircraft type provides insight into the platforms contributing to the reduction in flying hours, as well as the resulting change in funding levels from the increased utilization of higher-cost weapon systems. The following aircraft have reductions in flying hours: T-1A by (-25,318 hours), T-6A (-13,033 hours), HC-130J( -2,142 hours), KC- 46A (-2,000 hours), TH-1H (-602 hours), C-130J (-557 hours), T-53A (-440 hours), T-38C (-309 hours), UH-1N (-200 hours), T-41D (- 100 hours), T-51A (-100 hours), UV-18B (-100 hours), and the F-16D by (-87 hours). In contrast, the KC-135R increased by (80 hours), F-16C (101 hours), HH-60W (263 hours), C-17A (392 hours), T-7A (1,374 hours), F-35A (1,824 hours). The following aircraft had no changes: HH-60G, TG-15A, TG-15B, and TG-16A. Net adjustments in dollars may not always follow in the direction of the hour change due to price and consumption adjustments in the cost per flying hour rates for fuel, aircraft parts and supplies.

drivers.title: Transfer from Discretionary to Mandatory
drivers.description: Decrease in Flying Hour Program funding will be appropriately offset by funding sourced from the Reconciliation Bill (H.R.1) upon enactment.

drivers.title: Intercontinental Ballistic Missile Spares
drivers.description: Program increase is necessary for the Minuteman III Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM) program to maintain the viability and operational readiness of the current ballistic missile inventory. This funding request will provide the necessary resources for depot- level reparable and critical consumable parts, thereby sustaining the ICBM's vital role in strategic deterrence. Ultimately, contributing to the overall safety and security of the United States by maintaining the reliability and effectiveness of the nation's nuclear deterrent capabilities.

drivers.title: Efficiency - Contract Services
drivers.description: Reduces contracts for Advisory and Assistance Services to promote efficiencies and advance the policies of the Administration in alignment with Executive Order 14222, "Implementing the President's Department of Government Efficiency Cost Efficiency Initiative.

drivers.title: Transfer from Discretionary to Mandatory
drivers.description: Decrease in Global C3I and Early Warning funding will be appropriately offset by funding sourced from the Reconciliation Bill (H.R.1) upon enactment.

drivers.title: Global Command and Control - Aeronautical Safety of Navigation
drivers.description: Increase supports Air Force Aeronautical Safety of Navigation program, filling a significant gap in government-developed aeronautical navigation data by providing aircrew's access to a commercial library of data. Provides all-weather access to airfields worldwide via Instrument Flight Procedures (IFPs), data, and navigation charts, otherwise unavailable to aircrews. Funds fixed base aircrew navigation aids for Pacific Air Forces (PACAF), U.S. Air Forces in Europe (USAFE), and Air Education and Training Command (AETC).

drivers.title: Global Command and Control - Digital Infrastructure Sustainment
drivers.description: Increase supports sustainment of Digital Infrastructure Architecture, THRESHER, and accelerating Moving Target Indicator (MTI) processing. Funding improves the performance, efficiency, and effectiveness of digital systems and radar processing capabilities.

drivers.title: Nuclear Deterrence - Phoenix Air-to-Ground Communications Network
drivers.description: Increase supports Phoenix Air-to-Ground Communications Network (PAGCN) Expansion, which is part of on-going Nuclear Command, Control, and Communications (NC3) modernization programs efforts within the Department of Defense (DOD).

drivers.title: Global Command and Control - National Airborne Operations Center Reconstitution Team
drivers.description: Increase supports National Airborne Operations Center (NAOC) reconstitution team that will provide mission critical equipment to support continuity of government durability. A collaborative DoD and DAF effort resulted in several initiatives for E-4B to improve overall aircraft availability, maximize training opportunities, and maintain uninterrupted mission capability until a planned replacement aircraft is fielded.

drivers.title: Nuclear Deterrence - Nuclear Command, Control, and Communications
drivers.description: Increase supports Nuclear Command, Control, and Communications (NC3) to support Air Force Global Strike Command (AFGSC) priorities due to changes in requirements, modernizing sustainment and security operations, and the overall NC3 enterprise due to an continually-evolving threat.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Average Workyear Cost Adjustment
drivers.description: Increase in funding and manpower (31 FTEs) for Civilian Personnel compensation to adjust Full-Time Equivalent and average workyear costs. Each year, the Air Force uses detailed execution and cost factor analysis to realign and update civilian compensation costs and manpower for the purpose of accurately forecasting budget estimates for the civilian workforce. The Subactivity Group average cost adjustment is a result of these changes as well as updated pay raise, awards, and benefit assumptions.

drivers.title: Space Communications - Military Satellite Communications
drivers.description: Increase supports Furniture, Fixtures, and Equipment (FF&E) for Offutt AFB, Nebraska Military Satellite Communications (MILSATCOM) facility, relocation of Family of Advanced Beyond Line-of-Sight Terminals (FAB-T) and High-Altitude Electromagnetic Pulse (HEMP) Hardness Maintenance/Hardness Surveillance (HM/HS) support and sustainment.

drivers.title: Enhanced Theater Force Posture
drivers.description: Increase funding to provide necessary resources for theater posture in support of geographic combatant commander requirements. Funds the necessary operation and maintenance resources to sustain ongoing operations, support enhanced in- theater force protection requirements and maintain deterrence activities. In this Subactivity Group, funds global command control costs to include logistics, essential equipment and deployment travel expenses associated with the broader increased tempo and mission requirements in priority theaters.

drivers.title: Global Command and Control - 95th Wing Activation
drivers.description: Increase to fund the activation of the 95th Wing at Offutt AFB, Nebraska. This effort will enable effective command of forces to ensure readiness and deliver strategic capabilities to multiple Combatant Commands. This supports the Department of the Air Force’s Key decisions to reoptimize into an enterprise prepared for high-end conflicts and long-term strategic competition.

drivers.title: Efficiency - Travel
drivers.description: Reduces discretionary travel funding to align with Executive Order 14222, "Implementing the President's Department of Government Efficiency Cost Efficiency Initiative."

drivers.title: Disaster Relief Supplemental
drivers.description: Decrease funding for the one-time FY 2025 add from P.L. 118-58 Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2025.

drivers.title: Nuclear Deterrence - Nuclear Mission Sustainment
drivers.description: Increase supports Nuclear Command, Control, and Communications (NC3) to assure successful execution of command NC3 management, Defense Red Switch Network (DRSN) and aircrew alerting system sustainment. Assures support for the President of the U.S. (POTUS), Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff (CJCS) and Commander of U.S. Strategic Command (CMDR USSTRATCOM) nuclear command and control requirements.

drivers.title: Space Access - Ranges - Human Spaceflight Operations
drivers.description: Increase supports human spaceflight operations, specifically for space shuttle operations and critical contracted services related to those operations. This increase is aimed at ensuring the continued safe and successful operation of human spaceflight missions, including the space shuttle program, by providing the necessary funding for both internal operations and critical external support services.

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs - Other Theater Requirements and Related Missions
drivers.description: Increase funds for Global Command and Control requirements in support of Other Theater Requirements.

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs - Operation Enduring Sentinel (OES)
drivers.description: Decrease funds for Global Command and Control requirements in support of Operation Enduring Sentinel (OES).

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Realign MH-139 Manpower
drivers.description: Increase funding and manpower (6 FTEs) to realign manpower for MH-139 support functions.

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs - Operation Inherent Resolve (OIR)
drivers.description: Decrease funds for Weather requirements in support of Operation Inherent Resolve (OIR).

drivers.title: Efficiency - Contract Services
drivers.description: Reduces contracts for Advisory and Assistance Services to promote efficiencies and advance the policies of the Administration in alignment with Executive Order 14222, “Implementing the President’s Department of Government Efficiency Cost Efficiency Initiative.”

drivers.title: Enhanced Theater Force Posture
drivers.description: Increase funding to provide necessary resources for theater posture in support of geographic combatant commander requirements. Funds the necessary operation and maintenance resources to sustain ongoing operations, support enhanced in-theater force protection requirements and maintain deterrence activities. In this Subactivity Group, funds ISR support costs to include logistics, essential equipment, and deployment travel expenses associated with the broader increased tempo and mission requirements in priority theaters.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Efficiency - Workforce Optimization
drivers.description: Decrease funding and manpower (191 FTEs) to optimize the workforce in compliance with Executive Order 14210, "Implementing the President's Department of Government Efficiency Workforce Optimization Initiative."

drivers.title: Efficiency - Travel
drivers.description: Reduces discretionary travel funding to align with Executive Order 14222, "Implementing the President's Department of Government Efficiency Cost Efficiency Initiative.

drivers.title: ISR Support Activities - Proliferated Constellation Low-Earth Orbit (p-LEO)
drivers.description: Increase supports the Proliferated Constellation Low-Earth Orbit (p-LEO) integration as part of the Distributed Common Ground System (DCGS) network that will enhance intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities. The p-LEO integration supports the Air Force's Targeting and ISR Enterprise, specifically for Long-Range Kill Chain (LRKC) and Long-Range Fires (LRF) operations.

drivers.title: Other Support Activities - Joint Information Operations Warfare Center
drivers.description: Decrease funding for Joint Information Operations Warfare Center (JIOWC) to divest of service support to the Joint Staff, which includes reduced travel costs, equipment purchases, and other intra-governmental purchasing.

drivers.title: ISR Support Activities - Disposition of Forces
drivers.description: Increase supports Disposition of Forces (DOF) enhanced capabilities by developing comprehensive threat object data relationships and algorithms for target sets, as well as an object management system and compliant architecture. This will enable the use of Object-Based Production (OBP) to efficiently aggregate machine-readable information and provide dynamic custody of air and surface targets. The OBP-enabled system will accelerate kill chains through predictive analytics, leveraging significant intelligence community investment to deliver an enhanced DOF capability.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Warfare Center Consolidation
drivers.description: Decrease funding and manpower (67 FTEs) to divest and consolidate the capabilities of the Joint Information Operations Warfare Center (JIOWC) into the Joint Staff.

drivers.title: ISR Support Activities - Digital Infrastructure Architecture - THRESHER
drivers.description: Increase supports the development and upgrade of the Air Force's digital infrastructure, including the THRESHER architecture and the Multi-Spectral Test Infrastructure (MTI) processing system, to enhance its capabilities and ensure sustained operational effectiveness.

drivers.title: ISR Support Activities - Distributed Common Ground System (DCGS)
drivers.description: Increase supports the Distributed Common Ground System (DCGS), which is a network that provides intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) data to support military operations. Within DCGS, there's a subset called Planning and Direction, Collection, Processing and Exploitation Analysis and Dissemination (PCPAD). PCPAD is one of the Air Force's primary ISR core systems. The PCPAD system has equipment that requires regular maintenance to ensure it functions properly. This maintenance is crucial to support the global network and provide accurate and timely ISR data for: non-mission operational tasking’s (e.g., training, exercises) and mission operational tasking’s (e.g., combat, surveillance).

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs - Operation Enduring Sentinel (OES)
drivers.description: Increase funds for ISR Support Activities and Installation Operations and Security in support of Operation Enduring Sentinel (OES). This supports the five air bases in USCENTCOM and aligns to the current theater requirements.

drivers.title: Disaster Relief Supplemental
drivers.description: Decrease funding for the one-time FY 2025 add from P.L. 118-58 Disaster Relief Supplemental Appropriations Act, 2025.

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs - Operation Enduring Sentinel (OES) - Efficiency - Contract Services
drivers.description: Reduces contracts for Advisory and Assistance Services to promote efficiencies and advance the policies of the Administration in alignment with Executive Order 14222, “Implementing the President’s Department of Government Efficiency Cost Efficiency Initiative.”

drivers.title: Overseas Operations Costs - Operation Inherent Resolve (OIR) - Efficiency - Contract Services
drivers.description: Reduces contracts for Advisory and Assistance Services to promote efficiencies and advance the policies of the Administration in alignment with Executive Order 14222, “Implementing the President’s Department of Government Efficiency Cost Efficiency Initiative.”

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Classified Increase
drivers.description: Increase funding and manpower (20 FTEs) for Classified Program. Details will be provided under separate cover by the Office of the Secretary of Defense Special Access Program Central Office to properly cleared individuals on a need-to-know basis.

drivers.title: Command and Control Support Activities - Digital Decision Support Ecosystem
drivers.description: Increase supports Air Force Digital Decision Support Ecosystem, an Artificial Intelligence (AI) platform that provides dynamic tools to support strategic, operational, and tactical decision-making. drivers.description: Increase funds Second Destination Transportation (SDT) requirements, enabling global movement of munitions, engines, War Reserve Materiel, and classified assets. SDT supports over 26,000 annual shipments across 61 Air Force programs, sustaining operational plan execution and depot maintenance timelines. This increase begins to address a growing backlog of deferred transportation missions critical to theater access and posture due to persistent underfunding. This increase also restores a one-time $50,000 thousand execution year realignment in FY 2025 to fund an emerging must-pay bill. Lastly, the FY 2026 budget internally realigns a portion of SDT funding coded to support Overseas Operations Costs (OOC). The FY 2026 budget includes the internal realignment of funding from OOC to baseline program and the net effect is reflected here: Baseline Program $100,602 (FY 2025 Base: $117,584) Overseas Operations Costs -$50,003 (FY 2025 Base: $108,529)

Manpower will provide agile and expedited deployment by establishing intermediate staging locales to reduce delivery timelines and demand on inter-theater transportation during initial dispersed operations.
