drivers.description: Increase in funds for Air Force Post Office Mail requirements due to projected increase in mail volume and transportation costs. Enterprise Mail supplies worldwide mail transportation services for Department of the Air Force personnel and activities. Requirements fluctuate as a result of changing mission sets and global presence.

drivers.title: Logistics Information Technology - Transform Undergraduate Pilot Training
drivers.description: Increase in funds to execute a complete transformation of undergraduate pilot training (UPT). The revision includes expanded Initial Flight Training (IFT) / Fighter Bomber Fundamentals curriculum. Funding will transform IFT into Initial Pilot Training (IPT) by increasing the program hours resulting in graduates earning a Private Pilot Certificate, Instructor rating, and qualification on multiple engines. These training revisions will further cement the path to meeting the U.S. Air Force goal of producing 1,500 pilots annually.

drivers.title: Precision Attack Combat Forces - Indo-Pacific Command (INDOPACOM) Campaigning
drivers.description: Increase for INDOPACOM Campaigning supports the DAF’s campaigning in the Indo-Pacific effort by funding critical resources within the region, focusing on enhancing deterrence and defense capabilities across a chain of islands from Japan though Taiwan and the Philippines. This strategic requirement aims to prevent Chinese aggression by using advanced basing, distributed operations (i.e., Agile Combat Employment (ACE), etc.), and alliances to maintain a military imbalance favoring US and its partners in the region.

drivers.title: Precision Attack Combat Forces - B-21 Raider Beddown Support
drivers.description: Increase for the B-21 Raider Beddown supports the DAF’s effort to field next-generation weapon systems by funding the expansion for B-21 Raider operational beddown requirements to support the ongoing delivery of the new weapon systems, new operating locations and unit standup. Funding supports beddown requirements such as specialized equipment needs, facility furniture, fixtures, and equipment buildout, movement and relocation of people and equipment and airlift support. Funding will support beddown at the planned locations, Ellsworth AFB, South Dakota, Whiteman AFB, Missouri and Dyess AFB, Texas. The increased funding will enable the B-21 Raider to achieve its full potential and successfully support its critical mission objectives.

drivers.title: Nuclear Deterrence Combat Forces - MH-139 Helicopters
drivers.description: Increase for MH-139 Helicopters supports the DAF's effort to sustain the nuclear triad by funding the security and support missions that enable the triad. This increase supports the MH-139 Helicopters platform for day-to-day operational requirements. With the transition from the UH-1N platform, funding is invested to cover various expenses, including maintenance, fuel management, and training. This action will ensure the MH-139 platform can meet its operational requirements, such as nuclear surety support and other critical functions.

drivers.title: Combat Forces - B-1 Bomber Operations
drivers.description: Increases funds for the B-1B aircraft's squadron's operational requirements. This investment supports B-1B squadron's increased operational needs resulting from an increase in B-1B flying hours. The increased funding will cover the maintenance, sustainment and equipment costs; training range access; and weapon storage facilities across their two main operating bases. The B-1 is a key component of the U.S. Air Force's global strike capabilities, requiring robust infrastructure and resources to maintain its readiness and effectiveness in executing world-wide missions. These actions ensure the B-1 is strategically positioned to respond to global threats and supports a wide range of missions, from conventional strike operations to strategic deterrence.

drivers.title: Air Superiority Combat Forces - F-22 Training Support Squadron Relocation
drivers.description: Decrease following a one-time FY 2026 increase to support the movement of the 1st Training Support Squadron (1 TRSS) from Tyndall AFB, Florida to Joint Base Langley-Eustis, Virginia and includes the F-22 Formal Training Unit Mission Training Center breakdown, storage, movement and install at its new location at Joint Base Langley-Eustis. Additionally, the funding provided beddown support of the Langley Low Observable Composite Repair Facility for simulator instructors, communications equipment and other associated furniture, fixtures and equipment.

drivers.title: Nuclear Deterrence Combat Forces - U.S. Strategic Command (USSTRATCOM) Requirements
drivers.description: Increase supports USSTRATCOMwith a specific focus on equipment maintenance and the movement of personnel essential to its global mission. USSTRATCOM oversees strategic deterrence, nuclear operations, global strike, and other critical functions, making the readiness and mobility of its personnel and equipment vital to national and allied security. Funding will ensure mission-critical equipment is properly maintained to remain operational and reliable. This will also support transportation and deployment of personnel enabling rapid response to emerging threats, participation in joint exercises, and coordination with allied forces.

drivers.title: Nuclear Deterrence Combat Forces - Long Range Stand-Off (LRSO) Operational Beddown
drivers.description: Increase fully funds the Air Force Global Strike Command's (AFGSC) and the Air Force Installation Mission Support Command's operational expenses for the Air Force's LRSO beddown requirements. This investment sustains the U.S. commitment to maintaining a robust and modern nuclear enterprise and safeguarding national security. The increased funding will cover renovations and minor construction contracts. The increase in resources will ensure AFGSC can maintain a credible and effective nuclear deterrence as the LRSO enters Initial Operational Capability.

drivers.title: Nuclear Deterrence Combat Forces - Remote Visual Assessment (RVA)
drivers.description: Increase funding supports RVA security technology capabilities used for monitoring top-side activity at its various launch facilities. This technology also supports small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS) or drones, high-resolution cameras (augments reality and better depth perception), and remote sensing that can be used for infrastructure, evaluating airfields and support intelligence gathering.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Enhanced Performance Award Pool for DoW Civilian Employees
drivers.description: Increased funding strengthens the Department's ability to recognize and reward the civilian workforce whose expertise and continuity underpin mission success. Expanded award capacity helps retain the talent that sustains warfighter readiness, drives innovation, and ensures uninterrupted support across the enterprise. Investing in civilian recognition directly reinforces the workforce that delivers stability, operation excellence, and long-term capability for the Department.

drivers.title: Restore Primary Combat Forces and Support - Transfer from Discretionary to Mandatory
drivers.description: Reflects an increase in Primary Combat Forces and Support funding to restore baseline funding levels after a one-time decrease in FY 2026 due to a transfer of discretionary funding to be sourced from the Reconciliation Bill (Public Law No: 119-21 - One Big Beautiful Bill Act).

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Workforce Modernization
drivers.description: Decrease in funding and manpower (3 FTEs) reflects workforce modernization efforts to properly align civilian staffing to actual mission requirements within the DAF and to meet internal reorganization efforts and civilian workforce reforms.

drivers.title: ISR Combat Enhancement - Permissive Airborne ISR
drivers.description: Increases funds for the Permissive Airborne ISR, enhancing capabilities for Government Owned, Contractor Operated (GOCO) DHC- 8 aircraft for specialized missions which are critical for gathering actionable intelligence in low-threat or permissive environments. This investment strengthens the Air Force's abilities to conduct persistent surveillance, improve mission planning, and support a wide range of operations while maintaining a cost-effective approach in less contested environments. The increase funding will cover operational expenses for ISR platforms such as the MQ-9, ensuring they remain effective in providing high-resolution imagery, signals intelligence, and other critical data to inform decision-making and operational planning. Permissive Airborne ISR plays a vital role in monitoring adversary activities and enhancing situational awareness in regions where airspace access is uncontested. These capabilities involve the use of airborne platforms equipped with advanced sensors and communication systems to collect, process, and disseminate real-time intelligence.

drivers.title: Command and Control - Joint Simulation Environment (JSE)
drivers.description: Increase for JSE supports the DAF's effort to enhance high-end training and readiness by funding a cutting-edge virtual simulation platform designed to address critical gaps in current weapon testing and training infrastructure. The JSE provides a highly realistic and adaptable environment for simulating complex combat scenarios, enabling the U.S. military to test and refine advanced weapons systems, tactics, and operational strategies in ways that are not feasible with traditional methods. This funding will support the development, expansion, and sustainment of JSE assets and environments, ensuring the system remains capable of meeting evolving mission requirements. The JSE serves four essential functions: (1) integrated development and testing, allowing seamless evaluation of new systems in a controlled, simulated environment; (2) tactics development, enabling the creation and refinement of innovative combat strategies; (3) advanced training, providing warfighters with immersive, high-fidelity training experiences to prepare for real-world operations; and (4) systems experimentation, facilitating the exploration of emerging technologies and concepts. By investing in JSE enhancements, the military ensures a more efficient, cost-effective, and comprehensive approach to maintaining readiness and technological superiority.

drivers.title: Command and Control - U.S. Air Forces Southern (AFSOUTH) Support
drivers.description: Increase for AFSOUTH supports our effort to support multinational operations by funding it’s mobility and logistical support of its personnel. This will enhance AFSOUTH’s ability to maintain operational readiness, foster strong partnerships, and promote stability and security throughout the Western Hemisphere which is essential for executing its mission across Central and South America and the Caribbean.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Average Workyear Cost Adjustment
drivers.description: Increase funding in Civilian Personnel compensation adjusts average workyear costs. Each year, the Air Force uses detailed execution and cost factor analysis to realign and update civilian compensation costs and manpower for the purpose of accurately forecasting budget estimates for the civilian workforce. The Subactivity Group average cost adjustment is a result of these changes as well as updated pay raise, awards, and benefit assumptions.

drivers.title: Command and Control - Collaborative Combat Aircraft Operations
drivers.description: Increase for fleet readiness mission of Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) to support our effort to field next-generation weapon systems by funding the Mission Design Series (MDS) at Beale Air Force Base, California. This funding provides operational and maintenance support to ensure the readiness and reliability of the CCA fleet, sustainment activities to keep the aircraft and associated systems in optimal condition over their lifecycle; required renovations and upgrades to facilities ensuring that administration, secure spaces, and operational areas meet mission requirements, and furniture, fixtures, and equipment to outfit these spaces with the necessary tools and infrastructure to accommodate personnel and effective mission operations. Funding is critical to ensuring the operational success of the CCA mission, which involves integrating advanced unmanned and manned aircraft to enhance combat effectiveness, situational awareness, and mission flexibility. The CCA program represents a key step in modernizing air combat capabilities by leveraging autonomous systems to complement traditional aircraft in contested environments.

drivers.title: Command and Control - E-3 Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS)
drivers.description: Increases funds for the E-3 AWACS platform. This investment sustains the E-3's continued operational effectiveness through its ability to operate outside of contested environments and critical role to Airborne Battle Management, Command and Control, and Air Moving Target Indication Capabilities. The increased funding supports increased operational needs resulting from an increase in flying hours and will cover essential, daily operational expenses like personnel training, travel, and equipment maintenance. The increase in funds allows the E-3 to continue providing vital command and control to support military operations.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Workforce Modernization
drivers.description: Increase funding and manpower (294 FTEs) reflects the alignment of civilian staffing to validated mission requirements pursuant to Executive Order 14210, implementing the President’s Department of Government Efficiency Workforce Optimization Initiative and the March 2025 Deputy Secretary of War memorandum. The Air Force conducted comprehensive data-hygiene and manpower-validation efforts, resulting in a correction where FY2026 staffing levels were set below the Combat Enhancement Forces’ Program established requirements. The FY 2027 request reflects the full requirement necessary to support Combat Communications, TACS communication, Tactical Intelligence Cryptologic and ISR activities, and funds Air Force Special Operations and SOF capabilities.

drivers.title: Restore Combat Enhancement Forces - Transfer from Discretionary to Mandatory
drivers.description: Reflects an increase in Combat Enhancement Forces funding to restore baseline funding levels after a one-time decrease in FY 2026 due to a transfer of discretionary funding to be sourced from the Reconciliation Bill (Public Law No: 119-21 - One Big Beautiful Bill Act).

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Enhanced Performance Award Pool for DoW Civilian Employees
drivers.description: Increased funding strengthens the Department's ability to recognize and reward the civilian workforce whose expertise and continuity underpin mission success. Expanded award capacity helps retain the talent that sustains warfighter readiness, drives innovation, and ensures uninterrupted support across the enterprise. Investing in civilian recognition directly reinforces the workforce that delivers stability, operation excellence, and long-term capability for the Department.

drivers.title: Readiness Exercises - Combat Air Forces (CAF) Exercises
drivers.description: Increase for CAF exercises supports the DAF's effort to enhance high-end training and readiness by funding realistic, large-scale, and technologically advanced training exercises. This funding increase directly enables the "train as we fight" mentality to bolster the joint force lethality needed for strategic competition with near-peer adversaries. This increase enables the Air Force to forge a more cohesive fighting force by expanding its exercise program, including Large Force Exercises (LFE), in pursuit of readiness-enhancing venues and certification events to train alongside joint and allied forces for rapid, large-scale peer conflict. The LFE's will stress several theaters and Combatant Commands, on a global scope, focused on speed and scale that aligns with the demand faced during rapidly escalating crises.

drivers.title: Readiness Training - Pilot Production and Absorption
drivers.description: Increase for pilot production and absorption supports the DAF's effort to enhance high-end training and readiness by growing the Air Force fighter pilot workforce to meet operational demands and improve readiness levels in the face of increasing competitive global landscape. This funds additional basic course graduates from formal training units by hiring additional instructors, expanding training resources, and enhancing simulator and flight training capabilities. Additionally, this increase boosts combat readiness by improving pilot absorption, the process of integrating newly trained pilots into operational units, where they gain the experience and skills necessary to become fully mission-capable. This funding postures the Air Force to sustain its operational tempo, maintain air superiority, and meet the demands of modern and future combat environments.

drivers.title: Readiness Training - Enhanced Training Realism
drivers.description: Increase for Enhanced Training Realism supports the DAF's effort to enhance high-end training and readiness by funding advanced training programs and exercises at Nellis AFB, Nevada the premier training hub for the U.S. Air Force, to ensure pilots and aircrew develop the skills, tactics, and decision-making abilities needed to operate effectively against advanced, near-peer threats in highly contested environments. This funding restores a high level of combat realism to its schools, including the U.S. Air Force Weapons School and large-scale exercises such as Red Flag. Additionally, this supports the development and integration of advanced training systems, including state-of-the-art simulators, realistic threat emulators, and live, virtual, and constructive training environments. These enhancements will replicate the tactics, techniques, and technologies employed by near-peer adversaries, providing pilots with realistic and challenging scenarios that closely mirror modern combat conditions.

drivers.title: Efficiency - Contract Services
drivers.description: The reduction of funding for contract services is undertaken in direct support of the President’s executive order, which prioritizes cost efficiency, transparency, and the consolidation of services. This measure represents a deliberate workforce optimization strategy designed to streamline resources while safeguarding against adverse impacts to modernization initiatives and overall mission effectiveness.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Workforce Modernization
drivers.description: Increase funding and manpower (37 FTEs) reflects the alignment of civilian staffing to validated mission requirements pursuant to Executive Order 14210, implementing the Presidents Department of Government Efficiency Workforce Optimization Initiative and the March 2025 Deputy Secretary of War memorandum. The Air Force conducted comprehensive data-hygiene and manpower-validation efforts, resulting in a correction where FY2026 staffing levels were set below the Air Operations Training Program established requirements. The FY2027 request reflects the full requirement necessary to support mission execution and workforce modernization.

drivers.description: Increased funding strengthens the Department's ability to recognize and reward the civilian workforce whose expertise and continuity underpin mission success. Expanded award capacity helps retain the talent that sustains warfighter readiness, drives innovation, and ensures uninterrupted support across the enterprise. Investing in civilian recognition directly reinforces the workforce that delivers stability, operation excellence, and long-term capability for the Department.

drivers.description: Reflects an increase in Weapon System Sustainment funding to restore baseline funding levels after a decrease in FY 2026 due to a transfer of discretionary funding to be sourced from the Reconciliation Bill (Public Law No: 119-21 - One Big Beautiful Bill Act).

drivers.title: Command and Control - E-3
drivers.description: Increase the software and sustaining engineering requirements for the E-3, to prolong the lifespan of this critical airborne command and control platform. AWACS provides real-time situational awareness, battle management, and early warning capabilities, enabling the Air Force to maintain air superiority over the horizon in contested environments. This funding addresses increased costs to sustainment for depot-level maintenance, software upgrades, and the replacement of aging components to ensure mission readiness for continued fielding and sustainment of advanced air defense sensors that are critical to the North American Aerospace Defense Command (NORAD) Homeland Defense Mission. The emergence of new, unconventional airborne threats has intensified the need to expand sensor coverage and enhance early warning capabilities both domestically and abroad. This investment directly supports the warfighter and national security by improving the detection and tracking of low, slow, and other asymmetrical threats, which enhances the common air picture and enables a more effective defense.

drivers.title: Nuclear Deterrence Operations - B-2
drivers.description: Increase for the Spirit – B-2 supports our effort to sustain the nuclear triad by funding the B-2 sustainment. This funding ensures the sustainment of the nation’s premier long-range, low-observable, deep-penetrating strategic bomber, which supports the warfighter by enabling the destruction of the most heavily defended and high-value adversary targets. This investment addresses the growing complexity of maintaining the B-2’s unique low-observable characteristics, which are critical to penetrating advanced adversary defenses. As the fleet ages and threats evolve from recent operations, the requirement to sustain these capabilities has intensified, driving increased costs for depot-level maintenance, organic software sustainment, and the replacement of critical reparable components. The funding supports expanded programmed depot maintenance, accelerates critical aft deck repairs, and enables faster implementation of warfighter-submitted software change requests. These efforts directly enhance the B-2’s relevance in current operations to carry to the farthest distance, the heaviest ordinance than any other weapon in the department, all the while remaining a cornerstone of the U.S. nuclear triad. This investment aligns with the National Defense Strategy by prioritizing readiness to address high-end threats and hold our enemies at risk.

drivers.title: Nuclear Deterrence Operations - Minuteman III - Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM)
drivers.description: Increase for the Minuteman III ICBM ensures the sustainment of the ground-based leg of the nuclear triad, a cornerstone of the United States' safe, secure, and effective nuclear deterrent. This funding addresses the growing complexity and costs of sustaining the guidance system to proactively repairing test equipment of 60 stands, in addition to the normal Programmed Depot Maintenance (PDM), sustaining engineering to mitigate obsolescence, and operational software sustainment. It also addresses the refurbishment of an increasing number of field returns and funds the critical Integration Support Contract (ISC) to maintain system reliability to deter the only existential threat to the homeland. By ensuring the constant state of readiness of this vital strategic weapon system, the funding directly supports national security by providing a survivable, intercontinental nuclear deterrent and aligns with the National Defense Strategy's emphasis on strategic stability and deterrence.

drivers.title: Rapid Global Mobility - KC-135
drivers.description: Increase is driven by higher labor and material rates for the oldest tanker fleet during aircraft depot and heavy maintenance tasks. Specific depot maintenance activities include corrosion mitigation and engine overhauls, from over 60 years of continuous use during peacetime and contingencies. The KC-135 Stratotanker provides the most utilized aerial refueling capability for the joint and coalition Air Forces, during the transition of the full KC-46 fleet delivery for the U.S Air Force to execute global reach and power.

drivers.title: Combat Forces - B-1
drivers.description: Increase for B-1 Lancer supports our effort to ensure the continued readiness and effectiveness of this premier 4th generation bomber, a critical asset in the U.S. strategic arsenal with the largest internal payload of any active fleet. Recent inspections have revealed accelerated fatigue and stress on critical wing and fuselage components, requiring additional inspections, repairs, and potentially significant structural modifications. The B-1’s unique ability to penetrate advanced air defenses and deliver precision strikes across the globe makes it a cornerstone of U.S. power projection and a vital deterrent against adversaries. This funding supports essential sustainment efforts, addressing these structural concerns while enabling upgrades to critical systems, including low observation coatings, avionics, and mission systems. These enhancements will preserve the B-1’s survivability and lethality in contested environments, ensuring it remains capable of meeting evolving threats. This effort in sustainment aligns with the National Defense Strategy’s emphasis on readiness, modernization, and maintaining a credible strategic deterrent.

drivers.title: P.L. 119-75 - U-2 Depot Maintenance
drivers.description: Decrease in funding following a one-time increase provided in P.L. 119-75 FY 2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act - Depot.

drivers.title: Restore Real Property Maintenance - Transfer from Discretionary to Mandatory
drivers.description: Reflects an increase in Real Property Maintenance funding to restore baseline funding levels after a decrease in FY 2026 due to a transfer of discretionary funding to be sourced from the Reconciliation Bill (Public Law No: 119-21 - One Big Beautiful Bill Act).

drivers.title: Improving Unaccompanied Housing
drivers.description: Increases Unaccompanied Housing (UH) funding levels to continue providing support to the highest priority requirements and address findings from the Barracks Task Force. Improvements will increase quality of life standards, reduce issue response time, and address overall restoration and modernization projects to improve housing facilities in poor or failing conditions. The increase in facilities sustainment, restoration, and modernization addresses the deteriorating state of Air Force facilities by providing an enhanced level of sustainment for facilities as well as specifically targeting the restoration and modernization of dormitories to provide serviceable, quality housing to all Airmen. This is restoring Warrior Ethos by investing in the readiness of our facilities and improving the quality of life of our Airmen.

drivers.title: Demolition - Reducing Excess Infrastructure
drivers.description: Reflects a one-time programmatic increase in demolition focused funding to address the backlog of excess infrastructure in the Real Property Asset Database to eliminate degraded buildings currently consuming crucial resources.

drivers.title: Facilities Restoration and Modernization
drivers.description: Increase in funding to execute targeted restoration and modernization of failed or failing critical infrastructure, directly improving the condition, safety, and operational readiness of the Department's facility inventory. This investment ensures Air Force infrastructure is properly sustained, addressing the most urgent repair needs in alignment with the Infrastructure Investment Action Plan (I2AP) and DoW's strategic focus on facility sustainment. This is restoring Warrior Ethos by investing in the readiness of our facilities and improving the quality of life of our Airman and Guardians

drivers.title: Facilities Sustainment
drivers.description: Increase in funds to bring Facilities Sustainment to 93% funding level of FSM, greater than the 85% required through Consolidated Budget Review Guidance and in line with the Department's focus on adequately funding sustainment to reduce costly and avoidable Restoration and Modernization activity in the future, improving the overall condition of the Department's facility inventory.

drivers.title: P.L. 119-75 - Arctic FSRM
drivers.description: Decrease in funding following a one-time increase provided in P.L. 119-75 FY 2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act - Facilities Sustainment

drivers.title: Facilities Restoration and Modernization - Classified
drivers.description: Decrease to a classified program. Details provided under separate cover in the Classified Operation and Maintenance justification materials.

drivers.title: Facilities Restoration and Modernization - Child Development Center (CDC) Support
drivers.description: Decrease after a one-time increase in FY 2026 to provide dedicated funding for restoration and modernization of CDC facilities identified in poor to critical condition.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Workforce Modernization
drivers.description: Increased funding and manpower (213 FTEs) reflects the alignment of civilian staffing to validated mission requirements pursuant to Executive Order 14210, implementing the President’s Department of Government Efficiency Workforce Optimization Initiative and the March 2025 Deputy Secretary of War memorandum. The Air Force conducted comprehensive data-hygiene and manpower-validation efforts, resulting in a correction where FY2026 staffing levels were set below the Real Property Maintenance Program established requirements. The FY 2027 request reflects the full requirement necessary to support facilities sustainment of all Air Force installations and large life-cycle sustainment repair and demolition, restoration, and modernization for all Active Air Force MAJCOMs and USAFA. This program also includes critical maintenance of runways, utility systems, and facilities necessary to support flying operations.

drivers.title: P.L. 119-75 - Runway Repair
drivers.description: Decrease in funding following a one-time increase provided in P.L. 119-75 FY 2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act - Facility Restoration and Modernization

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Enhanced Performance Award Pool for DoW Civilian Employees
drivers.description: Increased funding strengthens the Department's ability to recognize and reward the civilian workforce whose expertise and continuity underpin mission success. Expanded award capacity helps retain the talent that sustains warfighter readiness, drives innovation, and ensures uninterrupted support across the enterprise. Investing in civilian recognition directly reinforces the workforce that delivers stability, operation excellence, and long-term capability for the Department.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Federal Employee Retirement System - Agency Contribution Rates Assumption
drivers.description: Decrease in funding to align with the adjusted Federal Employees Retirement System (FERS) contribution rates. These adjustments incorporate updated actuarial assumptions, workforce demographics shifts, and revised projections of retirement liabilities.

drivers.title: P.L. 119-75 - Emerging Technology
drivers.description: Decrease in funding following a one-time increase provided in P.L. 119-75 FY 2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act- Facility Restoration and Modernization

drivers.title: P.L. 119-75 - Facility Enhancements for Future Pilot Training Sites
drivers.description: Decrease in funding following a one-time increase provided in P.L. 119-75 FY 2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act - Facility Restoration and Modernization

drivers.title: Cyberspace Superiority - Air Force Intranet Control
drivers.description: Increase in funding is critical to the Air Force’s ability to operate, defend, and sustain its networks. Increased funding supports the retirement of legacy NIPR gateways and the installation of Next Generation Gateways (NGG) at 13 key locations, enabling DAF transition to a Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) in compliance with Executive Order 14028 and the DoW’s 2027 Zero Trust mandate. Key investments include; Splunk to increase capacity from 14TB to 20TB required for monitoring of USAF network traffic, other software solutions like Versa for virtual routers, Cribl for data logging, and the sustainment of Palo Alto firewalls across 150 bases to ensure robust perimeter defenses for the Air Force Network (AFNET). Modernizing cyberspace capabilities improves mission success rates for the Air Force’s ability to deter, detect, and defeat cyber threats from peer competitors, in the most contested domain.

drivers.title: Cyberspace Superiority - Air Force Cyber Defense
drivers.description: Increase funds for the software requirements provided by CLS and SE to accomplish the generation, projection, and sustainment of the only combat power to bring physical effects from the digital domain. This directly support 21st Century warfighters through secure and reliable conduct of both defensive and offensive cyber operations mission sets across cyberspace to prepare the battlefield, while disrupting enemy planning, reaction and execution. This funding expands configuration management, technical orders production, testing/validation and on-site squadron support on non-kinetic weapon system platforms that provide 24/7/365 monitoring and defense of U.S. Air Force Non-Secure Internet Protocol Router (NIPR)/Secret Internet Protocol Router (SIPR) computers, networks, and communications against hostile attack.

drivers.title: P.L. 119-75 - AI/ML for National Security
drivers.description: Decrease in funding following a one-time increase provided in P.L. 119-75 FY 2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act - AI/ML for national security.

drivers.title: P.L. 119-75 - Zero Trust Network Access Software
drivers.description: Decrease in funding following a one-time increase provided in P.L. 119-75 FY 2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act -Zero Trust network access software-defined perimeter cybersecurity.

drivers.title: Cyberspace Superiority - Distributed Cyber Warfare Operations
drivers.description: Increase funding to the Distributed Cyber Warfare Operations (DCWO) portfolio to expand tailorable architectures for Cyber Weapons such as; Infrastructure On Network (ION), Telephony Network Operations (TNO), and Off Network (OFFNET) to deliver non-kinetic effects solutions and payload delivery in all war-fighters’ theaters and every domain. These Cyber Warfare Mission Systems conduct cutting-edge capabilities for the warfighter, through agile end to end acquisition of software and hardware tests or repairs, at pace with adversary’s dynamic network and architecture developments.

drivers.title: P.L. 119-75 - Cyber Operations for Base Resilient Architecture
drivers.description: Decrease in funding following a one-time increase provided in P.L. 119-75 FY 2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act -Cyber Operations for Base Resilient Architecture.

drivers.title: Restore Weapon System Sustainment - Transfer from Discretionary to Mandatory
drivers.description: Reflects an increase in Weapon System Sustainment funding to restore baseline funding levels after a decrease in FY 2026 due to a transfer of discretionary funding to be sourced from the Reconciliation Bill (Public Law No: 119-21 - One Big Beautiful Bill Act).

drivers.title: Global Precision Attack - F-35
drivers.description: Increase for the F-35 is driven by increased requirements for Contractor Logistics Support (CLS) Spares and Maintenance intended to address material pricing updates, increased software requirements to address Flight test Support, additional Engines and Depot Level Reparable spare parts. As the premier 5th generation stealth fleet, the Air Force cost share of the Joint and Coalition program is determined by consumption and utilization. The Air Force receives more than 45 aircraft a year into the program, growing the active fleet by 5-9%, all while employing the current pool of inventory into the current contingencies world-wide. These investments into the core readiness accounts are essential in maintaining the F-35's technological advantage and ensuring its continued contribution to global precision attack in accordance with the National Defense Strategy.

drivers.title: Nuclear Deterrence Operations - Minuteman III
drivers.description: Increase for the Minuteman III – ICBM supports the DAF’s effort to sustain the nuclear triad by funding sustainment costs for ground- based leg of the triad. This funding will ensure the sustainment of a cornerstone of the United States' safe, secure, and effective nuclear deterrent. This funding addresses the growing complexity and costs of sustaining the guidance system to proactively repairing test equipment of 60 stands, in addition to the normal Programmed Depot Maintenance (PDM), Contract Sustainment Logistic (CLS) support to mitigate obsolescence, and Technical Orders (TO). It also addresses the refurbishment of an increasing number of field returns and funds the critical Integration Support Contract (ISC) to maintain system reliability to deter the only existential threat to the homeland. By ensuring the constant state of readiness of this vital strategic weapon system, the funding directly supports national security by providing a survivable, intercontinental nuclear deterrent and aligns with the National Defense Strategy’s emphasis on strategic stability and deterrence.

drivers.title: Air Superiority - F-22
drivers.description: Increase for the F-22 is required to continue addressing the escalated maintenance demands for Contractor Logistics Support (CLS) services that strip and reapply reversion-prone low observable coatings on the fleet. Funds the aircraft depot heavy maintenance and CLS spares to mitigate risks of diminishing sources. This expands the depot-level maintenance hours, and capacity throughput needed for individual parts, assemblies, or subassemblies based on historical data and contingency demands. The F-22 Raptor is the world’s first 5th generation fighter, capable of simultaneously conducting air-to-air and air-to-ground combat missions with near impunity in the most contested airspace. The F-22 program will continue growth in engines, contractor logistics support management, and sustaining engineering, congruent with increased use in current contingencies and to be ready for high-end threats.

drivers.title: P.L. 119-75 - U-2 Depot Maintenance
drivers.description: Decrease in funding following a one-time increase provided in P.L. 119-75 FY 2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act for Air Force Unfunded Requirement -U-2 Depot maintenance. 661 AF Consolidated Sustainment 930 Other Depot Maintenance

drivers.title: Mobility Air Forces
drivers.description: The Mobility Air Forces (MAF) flying hour program is the foundational enabler of global power projection, providing the United States with the strategic reach necessary to support integrated deterrence for Combat Forces. To build a resilient Joint Force prepared for strategic competition, increased funding is essential, particularly as the costs of fuel, parts, and complex sustainment continue to escalate. These flight hours are critical for mastering large-scale force employment and long-range precision strikes, which are vital for effective campaigning against pacing challenges. Without sufficient funding to meet these demands, pilot proficiency will decline, the combat radius of air and naval assets will be severely limited, and the ability to sustain the force will degrade, thereby curtailing strategic options in a global crisis. A ready and capable tanker fleet underpins the credibility of the entire Joint Force, directly addressing the National Defense Strategy's priority of deterring aggression, particularly in the Indo-Pacific. By ensuring aircrews are proficient in complex, contested environments, the U.S. demonstrates a strategic reach that complicates adversary planning and strengthens the assurance of our allies. This makes MAF readiness inseparably linked to the readiness of the entire Joint Force. Funding prioritizes the flying of our modern tanker fleet through the continued fielding of the KC-46A Pegasus while reinforcing the legacy KC-135R/T fleet. With enhanced capabilities in refueling, the KC-46A represents a significant leap forward in supporting operations within a contested environment. The combination of a modernized fleet and highly trained aircrews ensures the endurance required for any Joint Force package. Ultimately, this investment enhances the agility, lethality, and sustainment of the force. By enabling the rapid deployment and sustained employment of combat power, the MAF flying hour program is a critical element of deterrence, allowing the Joint Force to respond to crises with the speed, flexibility, and decisiveness required in a complex global security environment.

drivers.title: Combat Air Forces
drivers.description: The Combat Air Forces (CAF) flying hour program is a fundamental pillar of the National Defense Strategy, essential for realizing integrated deterrence and maintaining a combat-credible force. The program directly generates unrivaled pilot proficiency and combat lethality across our bomber and fighter fleets, ensuring our preparedness to deter aggression and prevail in conflict. Investment in flying hours provides the live-flying training necessary to hone advanced warfighting skills. Fighter crews develop proficiency in offensive counter-air, precision strike, and the suppression of enemy air defenses—capabilities that are critical for addressing the pacing challenge from the PRC and maintaining stability in the Indo-Pacific. Simultaneously, bomber crews maintain readiness for long-range strategic missions, ensuring a credible deterrent against attacks on the United States, our allies, and our partners. Funding for the flying hour program yields benefits across the Joint Force and the defense industrial base. It enables the execution of complex, multi-domain tactics in high-fidelity training environments, a critical component for effective campaigning and building a resilient, integrated force. Concurrently, such funding sustains the defense ecosystem by creating predictable demand for the spares and consumables required for sustained, high-tempo operations and surge capabilities. Ultimately, a fully funded flying hour program produces a more lethal, credible, and resilient force in direct alignment with core NDS priorities. It underpins the capability of our air forces to deliver overwhelming power, thereby guaranteeing the air dominance required to deter adversaries, defeat aggression, and provide the Joint Force with the freedom of action necessary to protect the homeland and our national interests. ($ In Thousands)

drivers.title: Formal Training
drivers.description: The Formal Training Program is the bedrock of airpower readiness, directly supporting the National Defense Strategy's imperatives to build a resilient Joint Force and enduring advantages. Defined by a "quality of hours" philosophy, every training hour is engineered to maximize combat skill retention, producing aviators prepared for high-end strategic competition. To meet the strategic goal of increased pilot production, a critical investment is required to cover the corresponding and escalating costs for fuel, spares, and consumables associated with a higher operational tempo. Investment in formal training prioritizes preparation for conflict against a pacing challenge by integrating our most advanced platforms into the curriculum. Flying missions in the F-35 Lightning II provides unparalleled, real-world experience, allowing new pilots to master the cognitive demands of sensor fusion, data management, and low-observable tactics. Hands-on experience in a networked, 5th- generation environment is critical for developing the tactical acumen required to dominate in highly contested, multi-domain environments and enhance the lethality of the entire Joint Force. Ultimately, a comprehensive training continuum that combines foundational airmanship with advanced, platform-specific experience produces a more lethal and adaptable aviator. The program is essential for generating warfighters capable of executing the complex demands of the National Defense Strategy, ensuring the United States maintains a decisive airpower advantage.

drivers.title: Restore Flying Hour Program - Transfer from Discretionary to Mandatory
drivers.description: Reflects an increase in flying hour program funding to restore baseline funding levels after a decrease in FY 2026 due to a transfer of discretionary funding to be sourced from the Reconciliation Bill (Public Law No: 119-21 - One Big Beautiful Bill Act).

drivers.title: Nuclear Deterrence - Survivable Airborne Operations Center (SAOC)
drivers.description: The Sustaining the Nuclear Triad effort is focused on maintaining and modernizing the nation’s strategic nuclear deterrent across its air, land, and sea-based components. A credible deterrent requires an equally survivable Command and Control (C2) system to lead it. Accordingly, this increase funds the critical SAOC and E-4B platform recapitalization. It ensures SAOC and E-4B remain on schedule and preserves the nation’s airborne strategic C2 capability. It further enables transition and bed-down actions, provides critical contract power manpower to reinforce an undermanned organic workforce, and supports security and base upgrades for the new weapon system, strengthening the Air Force’s survivable C2.

drivers.title: Global Command and Control - Backscatter Radar
drivers.description: The increased funding is allocated to sustain and enhance the high-frequency (HF), bistatic ionospheric backscatter radar system, which is critical for over-the-horizon (OTH) detection and tracking of air and surface targets across vast geographic areas. This advanced radar technology leverages the ionosphere to extend its range far beyond the line of sight, enabling the monitoring of activities and threats at distances that traditional radar systems cannot reach. The system provides long-range early detection, creating valuable decision space and enabling timely responses to potential threats. It will also fund the maintenance and sustainment of the radar infrastructure, ensuring its reliability and operational readiness.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Average Workyear Cost Adjustment
drivers.description: Decrease in civilian personnel compensation adjusts average workyear costs. Each year, The Air Force uses detailed execution and cost factor analysis to update civilian compensation costs for the purpose of accurately forecasting budget estimates for the civilian workforce. The Subactivity Group average cost adjustment is a result of these changes as well as updated pay raise, awards and benefit assumptions.

drivers.title: Restore Global C3I & Early Warning - Transfer from Discretionary to Mandatory
drivers.description: Reflects an increase in Global C3I & Early Warning funding to restore baseline funding levels after a one-time decrease in FY 2026 due to a transfer of discretionary funding to be sourced from the Reconciliation Bill (Public Law No: 119-21 - One Big Beautiful Bill Act).

drivers.title: Efficiency - Contract Services
drivers.description: The reduction of funding for contract services is undertaken in direct support of the President’s executive order, which prioritizes cost efficiency, transparency, and the consolidation of services. This measure represents a deliberate workforce optimization strategy designed to streamline resources while safeguarding against adverse impacts to modernization initiatives and overall mission effectiveness.

drivers.title: P.L. 119-75 - National Airborne Operations Center
drivers.description: Decrease in funding following a one-time increase provided in P.L. 119-75 FY 2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act - national airborne operations center aircraft availability rating.

drivers.title: Nuclear Deterrence - Strategic Mission Planning and Execution System (SMPES)
drivers.description: Increases sustainment efforts critical Nuclear Command, Control and Communications (NC2/NC3) mission-support capabilities enabling Combatant Commander of US Strategic Command (CDRUSSTRATCOM) to develop and execute Level 4 nuclear and conventional war plans, strategic deterrence options, and Global Strike missions. This supports Strategic Mission Planning and Execution System (SMPES) which integrates six legacy programs into a unified system-of-services delivering nuclear planning, analysis, and execution support for the CDRUSSTRATCOM.

drivers.title: P.L. 119-75 - Automated Cyber Operational Readiness Assessment Compliance Software
drivers.description: Decrease in funding following a one-time increase provided in P.L. 119-75 FY 2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act - automated cyber operational readiness assessment compliance software pilot projects.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Enhanced Performance Award Pool for DoW Civilian Employees
drivers.description: Increase strengthens the Department's ability to recognize and reward the civilian workforce whose expertise and continuity underpin mission success. Expanded award capacity helps retain the talent that sustains warfighter readiness, drives innovation, and ensures uninterrupted support across the enterprise. Investing in civilian recognition directly reinforces the workforce that delivers stability, operation excellence, and long-term capability for the Department.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - E-11 Restoral
drivers.description: Increase funding and manpower (16 FTEs). E-11 serves as a vital communications node, bridging communications between disparate ground and air units. The increase will to enable interoperability between multiple Tactical Data Networks, allowing information to be translated and shared across theater operations.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Workforce Modernization
drivers.description: Increased funding and manpower (35 FTEs) reflects the alignment of civilian staffing to validated mission requirements pursuant to Executive Order 14210, implementing the President’s Department of Government Efficiency Workforce Optimization Initiative and the March 2025 Deputy Secretary of War memorandum. The Air Force conducted comprehensive data-hygiene and manpower-validation efforts, resulting in a correction where FY2026 staffing levels were set below the Global C3I & Early Warning Program established requirements. The FY 2027 request reflects the full requirement necessary to support Air Force-wide Strategic Global Command, Control, Communication, and Intelligence with programs like North Warning System (NWS), North Atlantic Defense System, and the Integrated Tactical warning and Attack Assessment system.

drivers.title: Installation Operations and Security - Non-Kinetic Cruise Missile Defense Program
drivers.description: Increase supports Airbase Air Defense Systems (ABADS) Missile Defense program. Funds fielding and sustainment of supporting sensors, non-kinetic effectors, and other equipment for base defense at up to 30 hub and spoke critical sites across the US. This critical funding will ensure that these sites are properly equipped to defend against missile threats and protect the homeland.

drivers.title: Installation Operations and Security - Set the Theater (Pacific)
drivers.description: Increase for Set the Theater (Pacific) supports the DAF’s campaigning in the Indo-Pacific effort by funding Pacific Air Force's (PACAF) dispersal and Agile Combat Employment (ACE) efforts. This funding makes the required investments to prepare and sustain five additional clusters with mission ready material, storage, and sustainment, posturing for Air Force to support INDOPACOM operational requirements. Funding enables ACE operations in the first and second island chains. These efforts enable PACAF to be able to execute an ACE scheme of maneuver.

drivers.title: Installation Operations and Security - Combat Support Training Ranges
drivers.description: Increase supports efforts to build full operational capability to combat support training ranges, providing realistic environments for troops to train in critical functions like logistics, engineering, medical support, and base defense. Funding addresses equipment gaps by acquiring tools, vehicles, and systems to replicate battlefield conditions and improve training realism. This investment ensures state-of-the-art resources, enhances readiness, strengthens interoperability, and prepares personnel for the demands of modern warfare.

drivers.title: Efficiency - Contract Services
drivers.description: The reduction of funding for contract services is undertaken in direct support of the President’s executive order, which prioritizes cost efficiency, transparency, and the consolidation of services. This measure represents a deliberate workforce optimization strategy designed to streamline resources while safeguarding against adverse impacts to modernization initiatives and overall mission effectiveness.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Average Workyear Cost Adjustment
drivers.description: Increase in civilian personnel compensation adjusts average workyear costs. Each year, The Air Force uses detailed execution and cost factor analysis to update civilian compensation costs for the purpose of accurately forecasting budget estimates for the civilian workforce. The Subactivity Group average cost adjustment is a result of these changes as well as updated pay raise, awards and benefit assumptions.

drivers.title: Efficiency - Supplies and Materials
drivers.description: Reduces funding for supplies and materials to align with historical execution levels and ensure alignment with the priorities of the Secretary of War to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of our mission and business operations.

drivers.title: Efficiency - Travel Budget
drivers.description: Reduces discretionary travel funding to align with the Secretary of War’s highest priorities to strengthen readiness, modernize capabilities, and sustain the Force.

drivers.title: Command and Control Support Activities - Restore Rhombus Guardian
drivers.description: Increase supports restoral of configuration of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities and for Rhombus Guardian, a platform that provides AI-powered predictive and prescriptive decision support solutions for resources planning and programming. Funding will improve strategy for budget alignment, advanced data analytics, and strengthen the decision-making capability of our resourcing workforce. Additionally, the platform strengthens military readiness and lethality by delivering more agile, data-driven, and accurate planning, programming, budgeting, and execution (PPBE) analysis for decision-makers. The platform independently analyzes data, identifies issues, and recommends courses of action. This action will enable the AF to leverage advances in AI to optimize and accelerate resource and readiness decision-making in support of operational and strategic objectives.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Workforce Modernization
drivers.description: Increased funding and manpower (81 FTEs) reflects the alignment of civilian staffing to validated mission requirements pursuant to Executive Order 14210, implementing the President’s Department of Government Efficiency Workforce Optimization Initiative and the March 2025 Deputy Secretary of War memorandum. The Air Force conducted comprehensive data-hygiene and manpower-validation efforts, resulting in a correction where FY2026 staffing levels were set below the Other Combat Operations Support Program's established requirements. The FY 2027 request reflects the full requirement necessary to support combat evaluation groups and strategic missile evaluation squadrons; defensive training; civil engineer heavy repair squadrons (RED HORSE).

drivers.title: P.L. 119-75 - Foreign Ownership, Control, or Influence
drivers.description: Decrease in funding following a one-time increase provided in P.L. 119-75 FY 2026 Consolidated Appropriations Act for Air Force Unfunded Requirement - foreign ownership, control, or influence due diligence.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Enhanced Performance Award Pool for DoW Civilian Employees
drivers.description: Increased funding strengthens the Department's ability to recognize and reward the civilian workforce whose expertise and continuity underpin mission success. Expanded award capacity helps retain the talent that sustains warfighter readiness, drives innovation, and ensures uninterrupted support across the enterprise. Investing in civilian recognition directly reinforces the workforce that delivers stability, operation excellence, and long-term capability for the Department.

drivers.title: Defensive Cyberspace Operations - Information Technology (IT) Control Systems
drivers.description: Increase strengthens cybersecurity infrastructure for IT Control Systems, a critical investment to protect Defense Critical Infrastructure and ensure mission resilience. This funding mitigates vulnerabilities, safeguards homeland defense, and aligns with DAF Enterprise objectives by implementing robust authentication controls and leveraging cost-efficient Commercial Cloud Services. Mission Assurance - Cybersecurity (MA-CS) activities proactively reduce risks, ensure operational continuity, and meet Service responsibilities under DODD 3020.40 and DODI 3020.45. Additionally, this increase supports hardening legacy infrastructure to prevent mission disruptions and protect national security interests

drivers.title: Classified Programs
drivers.description: Increase to classified programs. Details will be provided under separate cover with the Classified Operation and Maintenance justification materials.

drivers.title: Efficiency - Contract Services
drivers.description: The reduction of funding for contract services is undertaken in direct support of the President’s executive order, which prioritizes cost efficiency, transparency, and the consolidation of services. This measure represents a deliberate workforce optimization strategy designed to streamline resources while safeguarding against adverse impacts to modernization initiatives and overall mission effectiveness.

drivers.title: Cyberspace Operations - Information Technology (IT)
drivers.description: Increase supports Information Technology (IT) infrastructure by investing in critical asset upgrades, improving end-user experience and enhancing network performance. Funding will support digital modernization initiatives, cloud transition efforts, and cybersecurity Zero Trust capabilities, providing secure access to data anytime and from any network. Increase also funds vulnerability management and IT security support ensuring IT policy-compliant network connectivity for communications across classified and unclassified networks.

drivers.title: Cyberspace Operations - Cybersecurity Service Provider Teams
drivers.description: Increase addresses a critical staffing shortage for the 16th Air Force cybersecurity mission. Funds provide additional contractor personnel for Cybersecurity Service Provider (CSSP) Teams for the Nuclear Command, Control, and Communications (NC3) mission and provides six additional Cyber Operational Readiness Assessment (CORA) teams. Increase also provides for additional travel, training and Information Technology (IT) equipment requirements commensurate with the increase in personnel. This budget supports the cybersecurity requirements that defend nuclear and IT systems and infrastructure, which are key to defending the homeland and deterring adversaries, as per the 2026 National Defense Strategy.

drivers.title: Cyberspace Operations - Post-Quantum Crypto Modernization
drivers.description: Increase for software-based solutions that will protect air-gapped systems, space/satellite assets and cloud environments to ensure the protection and enhancement of secure communications, Identification Friend or Foe (IFF), Nuclear Command, Control, and Communications (NC3), and other mission-critical capabilities against adversaries' leaps in quantum computing, which continually threaten encrypted communications. This budget ensures DAF cybersecurity capabilities remain at the leading edge, prepared and capable of denying adversaries' access to Air Force and Joint Force critical systems.

drivers.title: Cyberspace Activities - Cyber Training and Ranges
drivers.description: Funds increased Cyber Training and Range infrastructure and capacity (IT equipment, IT equipment maintenance and network connection fees) to meet training throughput requirements for the cyber Initial Qualification Training (IQT) and Initial Skills Training (IST) pipelines. This budget supports efforts to train the personnel needed in Cyber teams and positions to meet offensive and defensive cyber mission objectives. These training ranges provide hands-on realistic environments for testing, developing, and upskilling personnel against evolving threats.

drivers.title: Defensive Cyberspace Operations - Information Technology (IT)
drivers.description: This increase is critical for addressing the significant technical debt the Department of the Air Force has accumulated due to deferred investments in IT infrastructure and modernization. This deferment has led to degraded network performance and a diminished user experience, which directly impacts the operational effectiveness of our forces. This efforts are a necessary step to lay the foundation of our transition to a Zero Trust (ZT) security model, consistent with Executive Order 14028 "Improving the Nation's Cyber Security" and National Security Memorandum 8 directing ZT. drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Average Workyear Cost Adjustment
drivers.description: Increase funding in Civilian Personnel compensation adjusts average workyear costs. Each year Air Force uses detailed execution and cost factor analysis to update civilian compensation costs for the purpose of accurately forecasting budget estimates for the civilian workforce. The Subactivity Group average cost adjustment is a result of these cost changes as well as updated pay raise, awards, and benefit assumptions.

drivers.title: Efficiency - Contract Services
drivers.description: The reduction in funding for contract services is undertaken in direct support of the President's executive order, which prioritizes cost efficiency, transparency, and the consolidation of services. This measure represents a deliberate workforce optimization strategy designed to streamline resources while safeguarding against adverse impacts to modernization initiatives and overall mission effectiveness.

drivers.title: Efficiency - Travel Budget
drivers.description: Reduces discretionary travel funding to align with the Secretary of War's highest priorities to strengthen readiness, modernize capabilities, and sustain the Force.

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Enhanced Performance Award Pool for DoW Civilian Employees
drivers.description: Increased funding strengthens the Department's ability to recognize and reward the civilian workforce whose expertise and continuity underpin mission success. Expanded award capacity helps retain the talent that sustains warfighter readiness, drives innovation, and ensures uninterrupted support across the enterprise. Investing in civilian recognition directly reinforces the workforce that delivers stability, operation excellence, and long-term capability for the Department.

drivers.title: Personnel Security Investigations (PSI)
drivers.description: Increase to personnel security investigations to support growth in clearance and suitability requirements for priorities such as Nuclear Modernization, F-47, Golden Dome, and increased Air Force and Space Force end strength/accession goals.

drivers.title: Classified Programs
drivers.description: Net increase to classified program(s). Details will be provided under separate cover by the Office of the Secretary of War Special Access Program Central Office to properly cleared individuals on a need-to-know basis.

drivers.title: P.L. 119-75 - Classified

drivers.title: Civilian Pay - Workforce Modernization
drivers.description: Increase funding and manpower (54 FTEs) reflects the alignment of civilian staffing to validated mission requirements pursuant to Executive Order 14210, implementing the President’s Department of Government Efficiency Workforce Optimization Initiative and the March 2025 Deputy Secretary of War memorandum. The Air Force conducted comprehensive data-hygiene and manpower-validation efforts, resulting in a correction where FY2026 staffing levels were set below the Security Program established requirements. The FY2027 request reflects the full requirement necessary to support security programs that include Air Force Office of Special Investigations (OSI) and counterintelligence (CI).

paragraphs: Primary Combat Forces are comprised of three major subcategories: (1) fixed wing combat aircraft to include fighters, bombers, and strike assets; (2) nuclear assets to include Intercontinental Ballistic Missiles (ICBMs), the helicopters that support them and the bomber force's air launched missiles; and (3) conventional weapons that provide a strong capability to counter and deter a wide range of threats to the United States and its allies. Funds also pay for civilian personnel, support equipment and associated costs for wing headquarters, fighter squadrons, bomber squadrons, missile squadrons, organizational avionics and consolidated aircraft and missile maintenance. The objective is to increase readiness and functional proficiency through flying and ground operations training with personnel, equipment and systems that would respond to any war, crisis, contingency or emergency.

2021-011A.basis: FY2021 base-book narrative; combined base + OCO funding is reported separately.

paragraphs: Combat Enhancement Forces include Combat Communications; Command and Control operations; Electronic Warfare; Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) functions; Personnel Recovery and Special Operations Forces.
Combat Communications includes deployable Command, Control, and Communications systems and support combat communications units.

Command and Control funding supports Theater Air Control System (TACS) communications, Tactical Intelligence Cryptologic activities, Air Force Targeting Center, and the Air Force Modeling Simulation program. TACS provides the Joint Force Air Component Commander (JFACC) the ability to plan combined/joint theater air operations through the Air Operations Center (AOC) and perform decentralized execution of the Commander's intent. Components of the TACS include the AOC weapon system, Airborne Warning Control System, Joint Surveillance Target Attack Radar Systems, Control Reporting Center, Air Support Operations Center, Wing Operations Centers, and related command, control, communications computers (C4) capabilities. Battlefield Airborne Communications Node (BACN) provides an airborne, persistent and responsive combat network capability for voice and data to command and control centers. The Air Force Modeling Simulation program provides training tools for the warfighter including Distributed Mission Training Operations, Wargaming Simulation Centers, and the Air Force Agency for Modeling Simulation.

Electronic Warfare programs include EC-130H Compass Call aircraft, mission planning systems, electronic combat support, shore-based electronic warfare squadrons, combat identification, information warfare flights, and tactical electronic warfare equipment for multiple platforms. Electronic Warfare Integrated Reprogramming updates radar warning receivers based on threat changes, tactical electronic warfare equipment for multiple platforms, and tactical datalink support.

Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) functions include the U-2 Dragon and other manned reconnaissance aircraft, unmanned aircraft systems such as the MQ-9 Reaper and RQ-4 Global Hawk, as well as the Air Force Distributed Common Ground System (DCGS). Air Force DCGS tasks, processes, exploits, and distributes all the ISR collected by the various ISR platforms. Intelligence Cryptologic activities include near real-time intelligence broadcasts worldwide through the Integrated Broadcast Service. These systems provide an intelligence infrastructure to task, collect, process, exploit and disseminate intelligence products through the Air Force and support Combatant Command (CCMD) operations. The MQ-1 Predator was retired in December 2018.

Personnel Recovery (PR) funding includes active duty Air Reserve Component support for sustainment readiness of legacy HC-130J, HC-130N, HH-60G, HH-60W, and Guardian Angel (GA) units. In addition to funding operational PR units, funding also supports Civil Air Patrol operations, Aero-medical Evacuation units, National Security Preparedness programs, DoD Civil Search and Rescue, Isolated Personnel Reports (ISOPREP) related to Personnel Recovery Command and Control (PRC2) sustainment, the Joint Personnel Recovery Agency, and the Air Force Medical War Reserve Materiel contracts.

Air Force Special Operations funding supports multiple ongoing special operations programs and forces in support of Combatant Commands worldwide to include initial training and equipping of special tactics personnel, sustainment of Special Operations Forces (SOF), Battlefield Airmen, MC-130, AC-130 fleets, and vertical lift capability (CV-22).
In FY 2021, BACN funding was transferred to Subactivity Groups 12A Global C3I & Early Warning and 11W Contractor Logistics Support and System Support
FY 2020 Enacted Overseas Contingency Operations $1,014,170

2021-011C.basis: FY2021 base-book narrative; combined base + OCO funding is reported separately.

paragraphs: Air Operations Training consists of fighter initial combat mission training, advanced tactical training for aircrew, and missile launch training for ballistic missile crews. Funding supports training aircraft, aggressor squadron contract aircraft, training ranges, facilities, equipment, combat simulators, dissimilar air combat training (against different aircraft types), ground training munitions, training deployments, and exercises.

2021-011D.basis: FY2021 base-book narrative; combined base + OCO funding is reported separately.

paragraphs: The Air Force centrally manages and programs for Total Force weapon system sustainment requirements at the enterprise level. The Weapon System Sustainment (WSS) program includes Depot Purchased Equipment Maintenance (DPEM), Contractor Logistics Support (CLS), Sustaining Engineering (SE), Technical Orders (TO) and Cyber Sustainment. DPEM encompasses funding for required organic, contract and interservice depot level maintenance. CLS includes funding required for contract logistics support for a program, system, training system, equipment or item. CLS is used to provide all or part of the sustainment functions in alignment with an approved sustainment strategy. CLS functions include depot level maintenance, operating command organizational maintenance, repair, flying hours, materiel management, supply and repair parts management, configuration management, technical data management, sustaining engineering, training, distribution, and failure reporting and analysis. Though CLS is contracted maintenance, there is some organic depot maintenance work accomplished through partnerships and work-sharing (e.g., F-22 work at Ogden Air Logistics Complex (ALC), Utah and F119 engine overhauls at Oklahoma City ALC, Oklahoma). SE covers funding required for engineering efforts to review, assess, define, and resolve technical or supportability deficiencies revealed in fielded weapon systems. TOs include funding for up-to-date technical data used to sustain fielded weapon systems. Cyber Sustainment includes sustainment funding for cyber weapon systems. All DPEM is funded in SAG 11M. CLS, SE and TOs are funded in SAG 11W. Cyber sustainment is funded in SAG 11V.

2021-011M.basis: FY2021 base-book narrative; combined base + OCO funding is reported separately.

paragraphs: Facilities Sustainment and Restoration/Modernization (FSRM) functions include facility and infrastructure sustainment, restoration, modernization and demolition activities at all Air Force installations, including large life-cycle repair for all Active Force Major Commands and the United States Air Force Academy (USAFA). FSRM activities ensure installation facilities, utility systems, and infrastructure are capable of fully supporting mission requirements throughout their economic lives.

Sustainment is performed through a combination of organic workforce and contract support. Sustainment includes the maintenance and repair activities necessary to keep an inventory of facilities in good working order. It includes regularly scheduled adjustments and inspections, preventive maintenance tasks and emergency response and service calls for minor repairs. It also includes major repairs or replacement of facility components (usually accomplished by contract) that are expected to occur periodically throughout the life cycle of facilities. This work includes replacement, refinishing, repairing and replacement of heating and cooling systems, tile, carpeting, and similar types of work. It does not include environmental compliance costs, facility leases or other tasks associated with facilities operations (such as custodial services, grounds services, waste disposal and the provision of utilities).

The Department of Defense (DoD) Facilities Sustainment Model (FSM) is used as the standardized model for forecasting facilities sustainment resource requirements. The FSM uses the following formula to develop the sustainment requirement:
Annual sustainment requirement = facility quantity x sustainment cost factor x location factor x inflation
Facility quantity - the facility size expressed in the Facility Analysis Category (FAC) unit of measure (such as square feet)
Sustainment cost factor - the average annual unit cost (in current year dollars) for sustaining the average size facility in the given FAC
Location factor - a location adjustment based upon the local costs for labor, equipment, materials and currency exchange rates (overseas) compared with an overall base- city average

Inflation - factor to adjust current year prices to the target future year The Department uses a sustainment metric which is the comparison of sustainment funding to the requirement for a given year, expressed as a rate
Sustainment rate (%) = sustainment funding/FSM requirement

Restoration is the restoration of real property to such a condition that it may be used for its designated purpose. This includes repair or replacement work to restore facilities damaged by inadequate sustainment, excessive age, natural disaster, fire, accident or other causes.

Modernization is the alteration or replacement of facilities solely to implement new or higher standards, to accommodate new functions or to replace building components that typically last more than 50 years (such as the framework or foundation). Modernization also includes infrastructure repairs and minor construction to accommodate changes in mission requirements, including new mission beddown. Modernization is critical to ensure aging facilities remain capable of supporting mission requirements as they evolve over the long lives of facilities and infrastructure systems.
FY 2020 Enacted Overseas Contingency Operations $137,264

Recapitalization is the major renovation or reconstruction activities (including facility replacements) needed to keep existing facilities modern and relevant in an environment of changing standards and missions. Recapitalization extends the service life of facilities or restores lost service life. It includes restoration and modernization of existing facilities.
Plant Replacement Value (PRV) is used as the basis for generating recapitalization requirements. The Department of Defense standardized formula for calculating PRV is:

PRV = facility quantity x construction cost factor x location factor x Planning & Design (P&D) factor x historical factor x contingency factor x Supervision, Inspection and Overhead (SIOH) x inflation
Facility quantity - the facility size expressed in the FAC unit of measure (such as square feet)
Construction cost factor - the average annual unit cost (in current year dollars) for constructing the average size facility to current standards in the given FAC
Location factor - a location adjustment based upon the local costs for labor, equipment, materials and currency exchange rates (overseas) compared with an overall base- city average
P&D factor - an adjustment to account for typical project planning and design costs
Historical factor - an adjustment for historical architecture and materials (when applicable)
Contingency factor - an adjustment for typical contingency costs during construction
SIOH - an adjustment for supervision, inspection and overhead costs associated with construction management
Inflation - factor to adjust current year prices to the target future year

Demolition is performed primarily by contract. Facilities and infrastructure are demolished to free space for future construction and to eliminate obsolete facilities from the real property inventory. Demolition is a key component of the Air Force strategy to consolidate functions, vacate excess and obsolete facilities and focus sustainment,
FY 2020 Enacted Overseas Contingency Operations $137,264
restoration and modernization funding on facilities intended to function well into the future.

The most significant categories receiving this support are sustainment, restoration and modernization of real property, including: Aircraft maintenance and generation complexes Airfield runways, taxiways and ramps Critical infrastructure, including utility systems Command and control facilities Intelligence gathering and analysis facilities Dormitories and dining facilities Training ranges and supporting infrastructure Administrative support facilities for coalition partners

2021-011R.basis: FY2021 base-book narrative; combined base + OCO funding is reported separately.
